rule: Preserve the 201 features accepted in the confirmed ballot. For newer projects, queue ideas with more Want votes than Maybe and Skip combined. Previously excluded ideas require a new acceptance decision.

entries.title: Let the Boss Theme Play
entries.pitch: Pick duties where the game's own music matters, and XivPiano steps aside there: the radio pauses and the game's music comes back.
entries.how: In Plugin.OnUpdate, beside the cutscene pause, a 'step aside' check: ICondition BoundByDuty plus the duty's ContentType (from IDutyState and the ContentFinderCondition sheet) against a set in Configuration. It pauses with Radio.TogglePause like pausedForCutscene does, with its own flag. The music muting needs no change: OnUpdate already puts IsSndBgm back as it was whenever the radio stops playing.
entries.risks: A paused song's audio link can expire during a long raid, so resuming may skip to a fresh song; Radio already does that quietly. Two reasons to pause (a cutscene inside a duty) must not resume each other too early, so the flags need to be kept apart and tested.

entries.title: What Was That Song?
entries.pitch: A list of the last twenty songs, with thumbs, bookmark and 'why this song?' still working on them after they have finished.
entries.how: Radio already keeps the last Radio.HistoryLength (20) finished tracks in Radio.History. A History tab in MainWindow lists them with the same icon buttons as DrawControls; thumbs call PandoraClient.AddFeedbackAsync with the old track's StationId and Token (pianobar rates songs from its history the same way), and bookmarks and ExplainAsync take the Token as they do now. Album art reuses LoadArtAsync.
entries.risks: A thumb on an old song must go to the station it played on, which may not be the current one; Track.StationId has it, but the station token must be looked up. Pandora may refuse feedback on a very old track token, and the error has to read plainly. History is lost when the game closes unless it is saved.

entries.title: Hush the Orchestrion
entries.pitch: While an arcade panel has the focus, FFXIV's music fades down so the chiptune is the only soundtrack, and it fades back when you look away.
entries.how: PadCaptureService already decides five times a second, from GhosttyWire.FocusGet, whether the arcade panel has the focus. Feed the same signal to a small AudioDuck service that reads SoundBgm through Dalamud's IGameConfig once, lowers it in steps on the framework tick, and restores the remembered value on focus loss, every PadRelease reason and Dispose. A Configuration flag (on by default) and a /arcade duck toggle.
entries.risks: IGameConfig writes land in the player's real config, so a crash mid-duck leaves the music quiet on next launch; store the original in the plugin config and restore it on load. Players who already muted BGM must not have it turned back up. Focus detection depends on ghostty-dalamud and is not yet seen in game.

entries.title: The Veil
entries.pitch: One chord, or GPose starting, hides private panels and blanks window titles in the palette, taskbar and notifications.
entries.how: A Veiled flag in SessionService, set by a new KeyAction and by IClientState's GPose state. When set, PaletteEngine gets a context with titles masked, the Windows gate returns masked titles to the Umbra widget, SessionService.Notify drops names, and panels tagged private in Configuration are hidden through window.hide.
entries.risks: XivDesktop cannot mask the contents of a panel it hides late: anything captured in the first frame is already out. Other plugins drawing window titles are not covered. It must be clear this reduces exposure, not a guarantee.

entries.title: Pin This Spot as an Objective
entries.pitch: `/xivmcp quests here "Title"` records your zone, map coordinates, the current bell and weather as a new objective, and `export` writes the lot as a pack to share.
entries.how: ObjectiveCommands.cs gains 'here' and 'export' next to its ten verbs. 'here' reads the territory and player position as get_location does, converts to map x/y with the same maths as CoordinateProvider and set_map_flag, reads the live weather from WeatherManager and the Eorzea bell from the clock EorzeaTimeWindow uses, then builds the objective through ObjectiveFactory. 'export' serialises the store in the ObjectivePack format that load_objective_pack reads.
entries.risks: What time window to record is a guess: the current bell alone is too narrow, so it defaults to no time condition and says so. Weather in fixed-weather zones is reported as a problem by the evaluator, which is correct but surprising. Export paths under Wine need the same Z: mapping as load.

entries.title: Pending Approvals Where You Already Look
entries.pitch: Open approval tickets show as a single tracked line under the Duty List, so a request filed while you were away is noticed without opening the plugin window.
entries.how: APPROVALS.md names the hook: ApprovalQueue.Changed and Snapshot(). ObjectiveOverlay reads the pending count and the first two summaries (the existing approval sentences) and draws one entry; its click calls the same toggle as the XivMcp.ToggleWindow IPC gate with the Approvals tab selected.
entries.risks: Approving from a Duty List row would be one mis-click from an unintended teleport, so the row only opens the tab, and that has to stay true. Ticket reasons are client text and are shown only in the tab, not the overlay. Same unverified overlay placement as objectives.

entries.title: Quieter While Someone Speaks
entries.pitch: Lower the radio while a dialogue box is open, and bring it back up when the talking is over, instead of only pausing for full cutscenes.
entries.how: An IAddonLifecycle listener on the Talk addon (PostSetup and PreFinalize) sets a 'ducked' flag in Plugin. AudioOut.Volume is ramped over about 300 ms toward Config.Volume times a duck factor (Configuration.DuckTo, default 25%) from Plugin.OnUpdate, and back when the flag clears. AudioOut already applies Volume per sample in MpegSampleProvider.Read, so the ramp is a few lines.
entries.risks: The plugin cannot tell a voiced line from a silent one, so it ducks for every dialogue box; that has to be a setting. The ramp must never fight the volume slider in MainWindow. Talk is not the only dialogue addon (battle talk, some quest windows), so the first version will miss some.

entries.title: Share What's Playing
entries.pitch: One button copies a line about the song, with its Pandora link, ready to paste into party, FC or linkshell chat.
entries.how: A Share button in MainWindow.DrawControls builds the line from Radio.Current (Title, Artist, Album and DetailUrl, Pandora's page for the song, which Track already carries) and puts it on the clipboard with ImGui.SetClipboardText. A matching '/piano share' copies it too. Nothing is sent by the plugin: the player pastes it into whichever channel they choose.
entries.risks: Automatically posting to party or FC chat would be a plugin sending chat for you, which Square Enix's terms and Dalamud's rules frown on, so this only fills the clipboard. Some players will find the extra paste a nuisance, and that is the price. DetailUrl can be empty; the line must read well without it.

entries.title: Places You Keep
entries.pitch: Save where you stand under a name and point back at it later: /wayfinder save forge, /wayfinder go forge.
entries.how: WayfinderCommands.Parse gains save, go, forget and places verbs (they must be matched before the free-text zone words). Configuration stores a list of (name, territory, x, y, z); names compare through ZoneMatch.Fold so accents and case do not matter. 'go' sets explicitTarget exactly as SetMapTargetFromCommand does, with the name as the label, so arrival, the aetheryte hint and GetState all work unchanged.
entries.risks: A name that is also a zone name ('/wayfinder go limsa') needs a clear rule. Positions inside instanced housing are per ward and plot and would need those stored too, or be refused.

entries.title: Quiet While You Pull
entries.pitch: Almanac hides its window in combat and duties, holds any reply that finishes meanwhile, and tells you with a toast once you are out.
entries.how: Inject ICondition and IToastGui into the Plugin constructor beside ICommandManager and IFramework. On IFramework.Update, watch ConditionFlag.InCombat and BoundByDuty; set ChatWindow.IsOpen false and remember it was open. ChatSession keeps running on the thread pool as it does now; when it goes from Busy to idle during quiet mode, queue one toast for when the flags clear. A setting in SettingsWindow turns it off.
entries.risks: Some players want the window open in duties, such as for a crafting-log duty or a trial they have cleared many times, so it must be optional. Toast wording should not look like a game system message. Condition flags change briefly during cutscenes and zone loads and need a short debounce.

entries.title: A Voice per Thread
entries.pitch: Give each thread its own system prompt, so the crafting thread stays terse and the lore thread can talk like a Sharlayan librarian.
entries.how: AlmanacSettings.SystemPrompt is one global string and Engine.GetChatSession passes a Func<string> for it. Store a per-thread prompt in the kv table (thread.<id>.prompt) so no migration is needed, have ChatSession.SendAsync ask for the thread's prompt before the global one, and copy it in AlmanacStore.ForkThread. A few built-in voices ship beside DefaultSystemPrompt; the thread context menu in ChatWindow.DrawThreads picks one.
entries.risks: A voice that drops the default prompt's rules ('do not guess such facts', 'if an action is denied, do not retry') makes a small model worse at tools, so custom voices should be appended to those rules, not replace them. Voices that imitate named NPCs are fan content; keep the shipped ones generic.

entries.title: Play Journal
entries.pitch: Hours and sessions per game, from the play history the helper already records, shown on each cover and in a weekly chat line.
entries.how: The plays table in arcade.db already stores game_id, core, started and ended for every launch. build_state adds total seconds and session count per game to state.json; ArcadeGame gains two fields; ArcadeWindow's details strip prints them next to last played. A 'journal' verb in ArcadeCommands prints the summary to chat.
entries.risks: arcade.db is per machine, so hours played on the laptop are missing on the desktop unless a small per-machine journal file is put into the synced tree and merged. A crashed emulator leaves ended empty, so sessions need a sensible cap.

entries.title: Press the Chord to Bind It
entries.pitch: Record a key chord by pressing it in Settings, and be told straight away if Wine never delivered it.
entries.how: KeybindService already reads IKeyState with a GetAsyncKeyState fallback; add a capture mode that suspends ChordTracker, waits for the first non-modifier key and builds a KeyChord from the held modifiers, then writes it to Configuration.Keybinds through the existing SettingsWindow Keybinds tab. The timeout message is the useful part: it is the first direct evidence of whether Wine passes the modifier at all.
entries.risks: The game still acts on the keys while recording, so a chord bound to a game action fires once. Some compositors only drop Super on release. Cannot see what the game has bound without reading keybind data, so the conflict hint stays heuristic.

entries.title: The Chocobo Saddlebag Scratchpad
entries.pitch: A sway-style scratchpad: stow any panel out of sight with one chord and summon it back to your shoulder with another.
entries.how: Add a scratchpad as workspace 0 in WorkspaceModel (outside Count's 1-9), so Plan hides its panels regardless of the current workspace. Two new KeyAction entries in Core/Input/Keybinds.cs with defaults, handled in CommandRunner; summoning uses window.hide off plus window.toggle_pet or window.place with the configured PinArgs.
entries.risks: Needs window.hide from the newer Ghostty methods; on older backends it falls back to minimise or is unavailable. Workspace persistence must not treat 0 as an orphan to clean up.

entries.title: Glance at the Server Bar
entries.pitch: Hover the Lantern entry in the server info bar to see who is lit and their notes, without opening the window.
entries.how: Notifier already owns the IDtrBarEntry and refreshes its text on a timer from service.Friends and Book.TotalUnread. Set the entry's Tooltip to a short roster built by a pure function in XivLantern.Core (sorted online first, names through ChatText.Label, notes through ChatText.Preview) so it is host-tested. Clicking still calls toggleWindow.
entries.risks: Tooltips are SeString, so friend-typed names and notes must be escaped so they cannot inject payloads or colour codes. Long lists need a cap ('and 7 more'). Hidden while streaming would be a sensible option, since the bar is often on screen.

entries.title: Check It Is Really Them
entries.pitch: Four short words derived from both of your node ids that you can read to each other in game or in voice to confirm the friend is who they say.
entries.how: A pure function in XivLantern.Core over the two 32-byte node ids (sorted, hashed, mapped to a fixed wordlist), host-tested for symmetry. MainWindow's friend context menu shows it; a local Verified flag in Configuration adds a mark in DrawList. Display names are self-asserted (DESIGN.md), and friendship is keyed on the QUIC-authenticated NodeId, so this checks the thing that is actually authenticated.
entries.risks: Only as good as the out-of-band check; people will tick it without comparing. A friend who reinstalls gets a new NodeId and must be verified again, which is correct but will surprise them.

entries.title: Browse Pandora's Genre Stations
entries.pitch: A list of Pandora's own genre stations by category, to start one with a click when you do not know what you want.
entries.how: PandoraClient.GetGenreStationsAsync calls station.getGenreStations and returns categories of (name, stationToken). A 'Genres' tab in MainWindow lists them; picking one runs Radio.CreateAndPlayAsync with PandoraClient.CreateStationAsync on that genre station's token, the way pianobar makes a station from a genre. The list is cached for the session.
entries.risks: Pandora has changed its genre catalogue over the years and this call may return fewer genres than the web app shows. Each pick adds a station to the list, and Pandora caps how many stations you may have (PandoraException.StationLimit already explains it).

entries.title: Other Plugins Hear the Song Change
entries.pitch: Tell other plugins the moment the song changes, so XivMcp, Ghostty or a Stream Deck setup can react without asking every second.
entries.how: A message gate XivPiano.SongChanged next to the existing XivPiano.NowPlaying and XivPiano.Control, sent with ICallGateProvider.SendMessage from Plugin.OnUpdate where announcedToken already notices a new track, carrying the same JSON NowPlayingJson builds. XivMcp could add read and control tools that call NowPlaying and Control. Stream Deck works today through macros with /piano; the event is for plugins that show state.
entries.risks: Subscribers run on the framework thread, so a slow one would stall the game; the docs must say to return quickly. The JSON shape becomes a contract to keep. XivMcp's control tools would need the same in-game approval as its other actions.

entries.title: The Glove Warns of a Turn
entries.pitch: With vnavmesh, the glove taps twice and leans into the next leg a few yalms before the path turns a corner.
entries.how: Navmesh already exposes Corner and the path's corners. In Overlay.DrawWalk, when the flat distance to path[Corner] falls under about 3 yalms, blend the glove's angle towards the next segment and run Pulse.Tap at double rate for one period. PathFollow gains a small pure helper for 'approaching corner' so it can be host-tested next to MotionAndPathTests.
entries.risks: vnavmesh paths in towns have many short corners; the glove could fidget. Needs a minimum turn angle (say 30 degrees) before it warns. Not yet seen in game, like the rest of the path code.

entries.title: A Colour for Every Source
entries.pitch: The bead takes a different colour for your own target, the map flag and the quest step, so you always know which one it is following.
entries.how: Configuration gains a colour per TargetSource beside BeadColor (which stays the default for Explicit). Overlay.DrawBead and DrawTrail pick the colour from scene.Guide.Target.Source; a Pulse.Approach blend over about 0.4 s eases the change. SettingsWindow gets three colour pickers and a 'one colour for all' box. Colors.cs already has Pack and Lighten.
entries.risks: Three more colours to explain in a window that is already busy. Red and green as defaults would fail colour-blind players, so the defaults should differ in lightness too.

entries.title: Reference Pages
entries.pitch: Save a question you ask often as a named page and run it with one command or macro line, so your daily checks are one keypress.
entries.how: Store pages in the kv table under page.<name>. Plugin.OnCommand gains a 'page <name>' case that opens a fresh thread through ChatSession.New and sends the stored text via ChatWindow.Send. A small list in SettingsWindow edits them, and the transcript's context menu gets 'Save this question as a page'. Because it is a slash command it can sit in a game macro.
entries.risks: A page that asks for an action-tier tool will still stop for XivMcp's approval, which is correct but surprising in a macro. Pages run one at a time; a second while Busy is refused, as Almanac.Ask is today. It must never become a timer that runs itself.

entries.title: Right-Click Actions from the .desktop File
entries.pitch: Show each app's own [Desktop Action] entries, such as a new private window or a compose message, as palette row actions.
entries.how: DesktopEntryParser ignores every group but [Desktop Entry]; parse the listed Actions groups into DesktopEntry.Actions (name, Exec, Icon) and run each Exec through ExecLine like the main one. PaletteEngine.RowActions appends them after the built-in actions; LauncherWindow's context menu lists them under Launch. AppSummary gains an optional actions list, an additive change to IpcContract.
entries.risks: Chord assignment for arbitrary actions can collide with existing row keys, so only the first few get one. Some apps put odd things in actions that assume a running session bus.

entries.title: Apps on Your Hotbar, by Macro
entries.pitch: A palette action that copies a ready /desktop launch line for any app, so it can live in a user macro on your hotbar.
entries.how: PaletteCommand.Copy already exists and LauncherWindow already has 'Copy command'. Add a RowAction in PaletteEngine.RowActions that copies '/desktop launch <desktop-file id>'; the plugin's command handler already resolves ids first. The id is stable across rescans, unlike the name.
entries.risks: XivDesktop does not write the macro itself; touching the game's macro data is out of bounds, so the player pastes by hand. Macros are shared per character and can be synced; an id for an app you later remove just fails with a message.

entries.title: Friend Folders
entries.pitch: Sort friends into your own folders (static, FC, crafting pals) that collapse and show how many in each are lit.
entries.how: Groups are local only: a Dictionary<string, string> from node id to folder in Configuration, never sent to anyone. MainWindow.DrawList renders ImGui.CollapsingHeader per folder with an online count from service.Friends, and a right-click menu on a friend to move them. Mutes keep using the existing Muted keys, so a folder can be muted in one step by toggling each key.
entries.risks: Folders keyed by node id split when a friend reinstalls (new NodeId), until nostr device lists merge devices into one person. Drag and drop in Dalamud ImGui is fiddly; a context menu is the safer first cut.

entries.title: Away When You Walk Off
entries.pitch: Opt in, and your lantern dims to away after a few minutes with no keyboard or mouse input, and lights again when you come back.
entries.how: A Framework.Update tick in LanternService (it already polls lt_poll there) checks OS idle time through GetLastInputInfo, never game state, and calls SetPresence with LT_PRESENCE_AWAY once past a threshold set in Configuration, restoring the previous presence and note on input. Off by default, shown in DrawSettings with the other switches.
entries.risks: GetLastInputInfo under Wine reports X11/Wayland input only as well as Wine forwards it; controller-only players may look idle while playing. It must never override a status the player set by hand (busy, invisible), and the banned-API test in CoreTests must keep passing, so no IClientState shortcuts.

entries.title: Status Presets
entries.pitch: Save a handful of status-and-note pairs and switch between them with one click or one short command.
entries.how: Add a List<StatusPreset> (name, presence, note) to Configuration. Command.Parse gains an 'as <preset>' verb beside ParseStatus; Plugin.OnCommand resolves it and calls the existing LanternService.SetPresence. MainWindow.DrawMe gets a small preset combo next to the presence combo and note field. Parsing is BCL-only, so it is host-tested in XivLantern.Core.Tests like the rest of Commands.
entries.risks: Very little. Preset names must not collide with existing subcommands (on, off, invite), so they sit behind 'as'. Notes are still typed text and are clamped by the same length limit.

entries.title: Per-Client Call Meter
entries.pitch: The Status tab shows each connected client's calls per minute against the rate limit, and the long-missing rate-limit control lands under Advanced.
entries.how: TODO.md lists it: RateLimitPerMinute exists with no UI; add the input under Advanced in MainWindow.Settings.cs. The per-client bucket McpServer already keeps for RateLimitPerMinute and RateLimitBurst exposes its current fill, read by MainWindow.Status.cs as one bar per client, and get_server_info gains the same numbers.
entries.risks: Client names are self-reported unless a per-client token is used, so two clients can share a bar. Reading the buckets from the draw loop must not take the same lock the dispatch path holds.

entries.title: Explicit Content Filter
entries.pitch: Turn Pandora's explicit content filter on or off from XivPiano's settings, for streaming or a shared room.
entries.how: PandoraClient gains GetSettingsAsync (user.getSettings, reading isExplicitContentFilterEnabled) and ChangeSettingsAsync (user.changeSettings with isExplicitContentFilterEnabled), as pianobar's settings menu does; changeSettings wants the current username and password, which PandoraClient keeps for the session in its credentials field. A checkbox in MainWindow.DrawSettings, read after sign-in. Queued songs are dropped after a change so the filter applies from the next song.
entries.risks: It is an account setting, so it changes the Pandora app and website too. If the password was not kept, a change needs it typed again. Songs already fetched still play until the queue is refilled.

entries.title: Choose What Shuffle Mixes
entries.pitch: Tick which stations Shuffle draws from, the way Pandora's QuickMix lets you.
entries.how: Station already knows IsQuickMix. PandoraClient.GetStationsAsync would also read quickMixStationIds from the QuickMix station in the user.getStationList answer, and a new SetQuickMixAsync sends user.setQuickMix with the chosen quickMixStationIds, as pianobar does. MainWindow.DrawStations shows a checkbox per station when 'Edit Shuffle' is on.
entries.risks: Changes apply to the account everywhere, including the Pandora app, which is the point but should be said. The field is not present for every account type, so the checkboxes must hide when it is missing.

entries.title: Arrival and Change Events
entries.pitch: Tell other plugins when a target is reached or changes, so Ghostty, XivMcp or a macro plugin can react without polling GetState.
entries.how: Two message gates next to the existing four in IpcContract.cs: XivWayfinder.v1.Arrived (label, territory) and XivWayfinder.v1.StateChanged (the same JSON as WayfinderIpc.StateJson), sent with ICallGateProvider.SendMessage from Plugin.Update when the arrival timer fires or the guide kind or target changes. docs/IPC.md documents them, and the existing host test that checks every contract name is in the doc covers them.
entries.risks: StateChanged must be debounced or it fires every frame the distance changes. Subscribers run on the framework thread and a slow one could stall it; the docs must say to return quickly.

entries.title: Export a Thread for a Bug Report
entries.pitch: Save a thread as Markdown with its tool calls, model and settings, after a review step that blanks out names and tokens.
entries.how: AlmanacStore.Messages(threadId) already returns every message with tool calls and tool results. ChatSession.Render is the model for turning them into lines. Add a header with Engine.Version, engine.ModelLabel, ToolMode and ToolProfile, run a redaction pass seeded from get_player's result and the settings' URLs and tokens, and show the result in a window with per-line exclusion before writing it next to the plugin config directory.
entries.risks: Redaction by string match will miss things, such as a friend's name in a chat log a tool returned; the review step is the real safeguard and the README's warning about unreviewed transcripts still applies. The export must never include LeaderboardToken, AlmanacToken or XivMcpToken.

entries.title: Make a Shared Station Your Own
entries.pitch: Turn a station someone shared with you into your own copy, so your thumbs teach it and you can edit its seeds.
entries.how: Station already carries IsShared from user.getStationList. PandoraClient.TransformSharedStationAsync calls station.transformSharedStation with the stationToken, as pianobar does, and Radio replaces the station in Radio.Stations with the answer. MainWindow shows a small 'shared' tag and the button.
entries.risks: Few people use shared stations any more, so it is small value. The transformed station gets a new token, so LastStationId and any piano-duty-stations rules pointing at the old one need updating.

entries.title: Stage Directions in the Byte Stream
entries.pitch: A private `ESC _ ffxiv;` escape lets your scripts and TUIs cue real lights, bell rings, poses and camera moves on the same frame as the text they print.
entries.how: Profiles with `stage = true` set GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE and a 4 KiB OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES; libghostty-vt then hands over every APC it doesn't handle itself (kitty `G` and the glyph protocol stay internal), and the callback keeps only `ffxiv;v=1;` payloads. A new Lua hook, stage.cue(id, verbs), maps a whitelist onto what already exists: app/lights.nelua colour and intensity, bell.lua presets, world.place tint and backlight, anim_play, and showcase-style SetCameraState shots. While DATA_MODE reports synchronized output (2026), cues queue and fire when it clears, so a frame and its effect land together. An `ffxiv;q` probe is answered through the session's WRITE_PTY path so scripts can detect support, and a tiny `stage` shell helper ships beside ghostty-agent. Most of the APC-driven ideas in this batch stand on this plumbing.
entries.risks: Output is untrusted: an ssh session to a hostile box, or a log you cat, could flash lights or yank the camera, so it's off per profile by default, with a verb whitelist and a rate limit. Cues arriving in reattach replay are dropped, the way replayed bells already are. Camera and pose verbs are refused in combat, duties, cutscenes and GPose, and there will never be movement, targeting, chat or command verbs. tmux drops unknown APC unless allow-passthrough is on and the sequence is wrapped.

entries.title: Aetheryte Network for SSH
entries.pitch: Your ~/.ssh/config becomes a teleport menu, and connecting casts a client-side teleport that lands a shell beside you.
entries.how: New Nelua primitive ghostty.run(argv, cb) capture session plus ghostty.command(text). Agent-host helper prints TSV from `ssh -G`, `ssh-keygen -F` and a TCP connect time; tmux shards via ControlMaster only on expand. Lua menu in core/ui.nelua table widget; anim_play cast timeline, derez, open `ssh -t host` and pin as pet. No shim changes.
entries.risks: Can't hijack the real Teleport keybind. Probes can trip 2FA, fail2ban or slow DNS, so TCP connect only. Cast timeline must not lock movement. Real teleport VFX is research.

entries.title: Git Bisect, Heaven-on-High
entries.pitch: `git bisect` becomes a deep-dungeon descent, one floor per step, ending in a boss room where the first bad commit is waiting.
entries.how: A precmd hook, plus a `git` wrapper for run mode, checks for .git/BISECT_LOG. When it's there, the hook takes bisect_nr and bisect_steps from `git rev-list --bisect-vars` over the bad and good refs, reads the last verdict from `git bisect log`, and spots the `# first bad commit:` line that log gains when the hunt ends. It prints `ffxiv;bisect;floor=..;left=..;verdict=..` as an APC, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE (the Stage Directions plumbing). A new lua/bisect.lua maps good, bad and skip to cairn, trap and pomander effects built from bell.lua rings and the worldview glitch and derez, and on the boss floor pins a panel running `git show --stat` beside the pet.
entries.risks: It's a theme on top of real work. The precmd hook never fires inside `git bisect run`, so run mode depends on the wrapper. Floor estimates wobble with skips and merges. Deep Dungeon art is limited to game icons through ITextureProvider.GetFromGameIcon and colour. APC through tmux needs passthrough.

entries.title: Commands Cast Like Spells
entries.pitch: Long-running commands get an FFXIV cast bar and casting pose, and the exit code plays out as a spell effect.
entries.how: Agent parses OSC 133 C/D in the PTY stream and sends CMD_START/CMD_END frames; OSC 9;4 and 777 via libghostty callbacks as fallback. New lua/cast.lua keeps EWMA durations, a minimum threshold, and picks timelines played through anim_play. Cast bar and particles drawn with ImGui above the projected player. Exit 130 = interrupt. Chime needs a UIGlobals.PlaySoundEffect forward; VFX optional.
entries.risks: Needs shell integration on every host, tmux passthrough, and remote hooks over ssh. animation.lua's pose guard must yield during casts. Cast timelines vary by job and weapon state. Never touch ActionManager or the real _CastBar.

entries.title: Clipboard Crystals
entries.pitch: Every OSC 52 copy buds off the panel as an aether crystal that orbits you, and a remote program can read your clipboard only while you hold one out.
entries.how: Register GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_CLIPBOARD_WRITE: each GhosttyClipboardWrite carries MIME contents (OSC 52, OSC 1337 Copy or OSC 5522), the program name, granted and can_remember, and is answered inside the callback. Store the crystal (capped with OPT_CLIPBOARD_WRITE_MAX_BYTES) and mirror the chosen one to the desktop with the agent's existing CLIP_SET. OPT_CLIPBOARD_READ must also be answered synchronously, which the agent's round-trip CLIP_GET can't do but a crystal already in memory can: reply SUCCESS with the crystal you're holding out, otherwise DENIED plus a local toast. Dropping a crystal runs ghostty_paste_is_safe (bound today but unused), then ghostty_terminal_paste, so bracketed paste (2004) and kitty paste events (5522) are honoured. Crystals ride the pet springs in lua/world.lua; image/png writes wear a MIME badge until Kitty Graphics Tapestries brings texture upload.
entries.risks: OSC 52 read is a known way to steal a clipboard, so deny is the default and any remembered grant must be visible and revocable. Many apps never retry a denied read. Crystals hold secrets: memory only, cleared on logout, labels hidden in streamer mode. tmux needs `set-clipboard on`.

entries.title: Drive-In Cinema
entries.pitch: A cinema-sized curved panel on your island or house wall, lit by the game's sunset and rain, optionally broadcast read-only to opted-in friends.
entries.how: Solo works now: /term pin here plus lower pixels_per_yalm and a bigger curve radius; rain streaks from ghostty.env(); per-zone derez opt-out in worldview.nelua. Shared viewing (weeks, stretch): agent broadcast mode that streams output only and rejects DATA/OPEN/CLOSE, through a relay with per-invite keys, anchored by house ward/plot/room.
entries.risks: Truecolor text video repaints every cell and eats FPS; no kitty/sixel on the cell path. No depth, audio stays on the agent host. Agent token grants a shell today, so broadcast must be a separate read-only relay.

entries.title: Echo Replays
entries.pitch: Replay old terminal sessions as ghost holograms in the exact spot they happened, framed like the game's Echo visions.
entries.how: Agent records asciicast-style timestamped output and resizes plus territory and coordinates; REC_LIST/REC_OPEN/REC_CHUNK frames. Replay transport feeds Session:feed on a clock, reusing TermView and rendering. Keyframes every ~5s via libghostty formatter for seeking. Flash, rez-in and ghost tint reuse existing effects.
entries.risks: Recordings keep every token and hostname printed: retention limits, per-profile opt-out, playback redaction. Disk growth. Keyframes may not restore every mode exactly.

entries.title: Emoji Pyrotechnics
entries.pitch: Sparkle, party-popper and fire emoji printed by your tools burst out of their exact cell as particle effects that spill into the room.
entries.how: After Session:feed, walk the render state with ghostty_render_state_row_iterator_next_dirty and read GHOSTTY_RENDER_STATE_ROW_CELLS_DATA_GRAPHEMES_UTF8 per cell, matching a table in a new lua/pyro.lua that maps a grapheme to an emitter preset. Grapheme clustering (mode 2027) keeps ZWJ and VS16 sequences in one cell, so a flag or a skin-toned emoji is a single emitter. Each hit pins its row with a capped ghostty_terminal_grid_ref_track so redraws and scrolling don't refire it, and bursts during reattach replay are skipped the way core/bell.nelua skips replayed bells. Cell rects map to world space through world_transform_vertices; particles are quads through the depth-pass callbacks, landing at one Raycast per burst.
entries.risks: Dalamud's 16-bit ImWchar can't draw emoji outside the BMP, so most source cells still show tofu and the particles are shapes, not glyphs. Emoji-heavy output such as a gitmoji log needs a per-second budget. TUIs that clear and redraw make old emoji look new. Needs a photosensitivity switch, and emitters stay off in duties.

entries.title: Glyphfall
entries.pitch: Lines that scroll off a world panel fall out of it as real letters that splash in rain, drift in snow and pile up at your feet until you clear the screen.
entries.how: The core keeps a tracked grid ref on the top row of the active area; after new output, that ref's SCREEN position against DATA_SCROLLBACK_ROWS says how many rows just scrolled off, which keeps working once the 10,000-line scrollback is full and the row count stops growing. Each new history row is read back with ghostty_terminal_grid_ref at a HISTORY point plus ghostty_grid_ref_graphemes and ghostty_grid_ref_style, and every non-blank glyph spawns a particle at its cell's spot on the panel's top edge. One Raycast per batch finds the ground, a cheap integrator moves the letters, and they're drawn with PushWorldFont AddText. A new lua/glyphfall.lua turns the ghostty.env() weather id into behaviour: rain splashes and fades, snow drifts and piles, wind and sand push sideways. An empty viewport right after output triggers the sweep.
entries.risks: Fast output means thousands of letters a second, so it needs a hard particle cap, sampling of every Nth row and whole-line strips as a fallback. ImGui letters ignore depth unless routed through the depth pass, so piles show through walls. Alt-screen TUIs never scroll into history, so htop never snows. Weather ids need a hand-made table, and house interiors have no weather. It's decoration, not a log.

entries.title: /grep the World
entries.pitch: One scrollback search across every terminal you own, with hit counts floating over panels and 'next' flying the camera to the match.
entries.how: libghostty-vt ships vt/search.h with incremental feed/tick across screens and scrollback. One GhosttySearch per Session, a few ticks per frame. Highlight as selection, scroll via scroll_delta, badges projected in draw_world, counts in the Umbra popup for minimized tabs. Camera reuses fly-in easing; prompt stepping via SEMANTIC_PROMPT.
entries.risks: Sleeping panels only retain the 256 KiB replay ring; search agent-side or say so plainly. Byte-exact matching, no regex. Prompt stepping needs shell integration.

entries.title: Saucer Arcade Cabinets
entries.pitch: Real terminal games run in glowing arcade cabinets along your house wall or beside the Gold Saucer's own machines, with a high-score marquee only you can see.
entries.how: Each cabinet is a world panel pinned with `/term pin here` using a profile whose command is the game (crawl, nethack, bastet, tint, moon-buggy, ninvaders). A Lua `cabinet` place() shape tilts the panel back, adds a marquee strip and turns the backlight and light_intensity up. Double-click fly-in already exists. While a cabinet has focus, a keymap mode maps GamepadPressed buttons to arrows and letters through the key encoder with setopt_from_terminal, so DECCKM and kitty flags stay right. The core reads DATA_MODE for synchronized output (2026) and skips render_state_update between begin and end, so fast redraws never tear. The marquee flourish comes from a score-file watcher on the host that writes an `ffxiv;score` APC.
entries.risks: Dalamud can read gamepad state but can't reliably swallow it, so the stick may still walk your character; keyboard or unused buttons are safer. In the crowded Gold Saucer panels without a working depth test cover other players in your view. 80x24 roguelikes need a readable pixels_per_yalm at fly-in size. Scores are local and easy to fake, which is fine because nothing is shared. It never touches MGP or the real minigames.

entries.title: Sit Down to Work
entries.pitch: Sit in any chair and your panels swing into a seated three-monitor arc while the camera settles into first person.
entries.how: Detect chair sit from ghostty.anim_state() Mode/ModeParam (or forward EmoteController id). Lua 'desk' layout computes arc slots from seated position and heading and springs anchors there. Camera reuses the double-click Get/SetCameraState path, written once and restored once. Model M joins when it lands.
entries.risks: Tablet/typing pose overrides may knock you out of the chair, so disable them while seated. First-person near-plane clipping. Triggers in inns and public chairs unless limited to housing.

entries.title: Agent Progress as Tracked Quests
entries.pitch: The agent board's running entries appear under the Duty List next to custom objectives, with a progress line and a quest toast when one finishes.
entries.how: ObjectiveOverlay already draws native-styled rows under DutyListAnchor. A second section reads AgentBoard (subscribing to its change event as the IPC Changed gate does) and draws each running post as title plus status line, with the Progress value as a thin bar in the Duty List's colours. Done and Failed transitions call IToastGui.ShowQuest as ObjectiveTracker does. A Settings toggle beside 'Custom objectives' chooses board, objectives or both.
entries.risks: The overlay itself has never been seen in game (OBJECTIVES.md checklist), so this inherits every placement question. Five busy agents crowd the Duty List; it needs a cap and collapse. Agent names and status text are client-supplied and must be length-capped and cleaned before drawing.

entries.title: A Station for Every Place
entries.pitch: Tie a station to a zone, a kind of duty or your home, so the radio changes with where you are and goes back when you leave.
entries.how: Configuration gains a list of rules (territory id, or a content type from the ContentFinderCondition sheet, or 'housing') to a station Id, like LastStationId. Plugin subscribes to IClientState.TerritoryChanged and IDutyState.DutyStarted, finds the first matching rule, and calls Radio.PlayStationAsync through Plugin.Run with the matching entry of Radio.Stations. The station before the rule is remembered and restored when no rule matches. MainWindow gets a 'Stations for places' section with a 'this zone' button that fills in IClientState.TerritoryType. Zone names come from the TerritoryType sheet through IDataManager.
entries.risks: Switching stations throws away the current song and fetches a fresh playlist, so rapid zoning (a housing ward tour) would burn through songs; switches need a short settle time. A rule pointing at a station you deleted must fail quietly. Pandora limits how many songs you may skip an hour on some accounts, and changing station is not a skip, but it should be checked.

entries.title: Aetheryte Uplink
entries.pitch: Aetherytes become status beacons for your hosts, and teleporting dissolves your terminals into aether that rebuilds on arrival.
entries.how: Shim adds FindNearest(Aetheryte) from IObjectTable. Lua reuses place_pet orbit math; worldview.nelua draws rings and halo. Host data from the shared probe/EVENT feed. Shim forwards Casting and BetweenAreas; worldview runs combat derez in reverse with a screen-space stream during loading and a line-reveal on arrival.
entries.risks: Halo is faked, not a real crystal tint; rings draw through geometry. Teleport detection is heuristic (Return, duty transitions). Needs a hide-hostnames option on stream.

entries.title: Apps That Follow the Sun
entries.pitch: The terminal tells your apps it's light mode at Eorzean dawn and dark mode at dusk, so their themes change as the sun comes up over Thanalan.
entries.how: A Lua hook scheme.decide(env) reads ghostty.env() (day seconds, rain, weather id) plus an indoors flag the shim would add from TerritoryType, and returns light or dark with hysteresis. Sessions register GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_COLOR_SCHEME so `CSI ? 996 n` queries get the current answer. When the answer flips, every session whose DATA_MODE shows 2031 gets an unsolicited report from ghostty_color_scheme_report_encode written to the PTY. OPT_COLOR_BACKGROUND, FOREGROUND and PALETTE switch to dawn and dusk sets built with ghostty_color_palette_generate and clamped with ghostty_color_contrast, so tools that only query OSC 10/11 at startup get the right colours next launch. Sleeping panels get the latest report on wake.
entries.risks: Mode 2031 support is uneven, and many tools read OSC 11 once and never again. A mid-session flip can be jarring, so it's per profile with a manual override and flips at most once per Eorzean hour (about three real minutes). Reports only go to apps that enabled 2031, never into a bare prompt. Soul Crystal Themes recolours the terminal; this tells the apps.

entries.title: Emotes as a Window Manager
entries.pitch: /beckon calls a panel over, /point focuses one, /shoo minimizes it, and bound emotes run commands after confirmation.
entries.how: anim_state() already returns TimelineIds[0]; lua/emotes.lua maps emote timeline ids to actions on rising edge. Point picks the smallest angle off facing. Bound commands go through sendtext.nelua. Sigil is a projected ImGui ellipse. EmoteController.EmoteId forward as backup.
entries.risks: Pose guard eats emotes within 0.1s, so whitelist them. Confirmation is mandatory and binds default read-only. Slower than hotkeys; mostly for fun.

entries.title: Save Timeline
entries.pitch: A history strip for each game showing every pre-launch backup and synced version, with one button to go back.
entries.how: backup_saves already keeps the last 10 copies under backups/<game>/<time>/, and Syncthing keeps .stversions in the synced tree. A new helper verb 'history <game>' lists both into state.json, and 'restore <game> <stamp>' runs settle() first, then backup_saves on the current files, then copies through the same never-lose rules as copy_if_newer, forced for this one explicit choice. ArcadeWindow's details strip gets a History button next to Play.
entries.risks: Restoring while another machine is playing just creates a conflict, so it must refuse while sync says Syncing or the game is running. Standalone memory cards hold many games at once, so restoring one card rolls back every game on it; the window has to say so. Staggered versioning names are Syncthing's own format and may change.

entries.title: Stow the Desk When the Duty Pops
entries.pitch: When you enter a duty or combat starts, hide every window panel, and put them back exactly as they were when it ends.
entries.how: Plugin.cs already receives ICondition (AskService uses it). A DutyGuard in SessionService watches BoundByDuty and InCombat with a short settle delay, remembers WorkspaceModel's state, and hides everything through the same Plan and window.hide path workspaces use; the exit restores it. Per-condition toggles in Settings, General, plus an exception list for apps the player wants kept, such as voice chat.
entries.risks: Hiding is presentation only: a video keeps playing and audio keeps going. If a panel owns the keyboard when a pull starts, focus must return to the game first or it is dangerous. Condition flags flicker around cutscenes and zoning, so a naive watcher will thrash.

entries.title: Change Job, Change Desk
entries.pitch: Link a gearset or job to a workspace, so switching to a crafter brings the crafting spreadsheet and switching to a tank brings the raid notes.
entries.how: Poll the local player's ClassJob once per frame in the IFramework.Update tick KeybindService already runs, or on a class-change event where Dalamud offers one. A Configuration map from ClassJob row id to workspace number, applied through SessionService's existing workspace switch and WorkspaceModel.Plan. Only the player's own job is read.
entries.risks: Fast gear swaps must be debounced. Switching workspace hides panels; a hidden video keeps playing sound, so this can surprise. Must never fire in a duty unless enabled separately.

entries.title: Approvals That Wait for the Pull to End
entries.pitch: An agent's gated call that arrives mid-fight becomes a ticket instead of a prompt, and the prompt appears once you are out of combat.
entries.how: ConfirmationService.ApproveToolCallAsync reads ICondition first: while InCombat (or BoundByDuty with the duty started, the flags get_conditions and get_duty_state already read) it does not open ConfirmWindow but files the call through the same path request_action uses into ApprovalQueue/TicketStore, and the tools/call answers with the ticket id so the client can follow the resume contract in APPROVALS.md. ApprovalWiring's 1 Hz tick raises the toast when the condition clears. A setting under Advanced in MainWindow.Settings.cs turns it off.
entries.risks: Clients that do not implement the ticket resume contract see a call that never completes, so the answer must say plainly what happened. The 20-second prompt timeout and the call timeout both need rethinking for this path. Condition flags are among the ClientStructs members not yet observed in game. With approval switched off it changes nothing, which is correct but should be said in the setting's text.

entries.title: Add Variety to a Station
entries.pitch: See what a station is built from, add an artist or song to it, and take back a thumb you regret, without leaving the game.
entries.how: PandoraClient gains GetStationAsync (station.getStation with includeExtendedAttributes, returning seeds and feedback), AddMusicAsync (station.addMusic with a musicToken from SearchAsync), DeleteMusicAsync (station.deleteMusic with the seedId) and DeleteFeedbackAsync (station.deleteFeedback with the feedbackId), the calls pianobar makes in src/libpiano/request.c. MainWindow gets a 'Station details' popup reusing the search box from DrawNewStation. Host tests go into PandoraTests against the fake Pandora.
entries.risks: More Pandora calls means more of an unofficial API to keep working. A station must keep at least one seed, and Pandora's answer to removing the last must read clearly. Shared stations cannot be edited until they are made your own (piano-adopt-shared).

entries.title: A Queue of Stops
entries.pitch: Line up several targets and walk them in order: each one is dropped as you reach it and the bead turns to the next.
entries.how: Plugin.explicitTarget becomes the head of an immutable list swapped atomically (IPC callers are on other threads). The existing ArrivalTimer and ClearOnArrival logic pop the head instead of clearing. New verbs in Commands.cs: add, next, skip, list. A new IPC function XivWayfinder.v1.AddTarget sits beside SetTarget in IpcContract.cs and docs/IPC.md; GetState gains a 'queue' count, which is additive and keeps version 1.
entries.risks: The order is yours, not an optimised route; people will ask for 'shortest order', which is a travelling-salesman problem across zones. Queue and single-target semantics must stay obvious: does SetTarget replace the whole queue? It should, and the docs must say so.

entries.title: The Engine's Knowledge in Game
entries.pitch: When the plugin already uses an Almanac gateway, also offer the engine's read-only tools, such as kb_search and model_residency, in the in-game chat.
entries.how: ToolHub already merges several sources, first-lister wins. When AlmanacSettings.Engine == EngineAlmanac, create a second McpToolSource over McpHttpClient pointed at the engine's MCP port (41880) with AlmanacToken and id "almanac", and add it after XivMcp in Engine.NewLoop. Filter to tools whose safety is read, since the engine's change tools rely on MCP elicitation or confirm tokens the chat window does not implement.
entries.risks: The engine's gateway and MCP server are separate listeners with the same bearer token; a player who exposed one but not the other gets a confusing half-connection. Tool names may collide with XivMcp's, so the engine's need a prefix. Engine tools that run commands on remote hosts should stay out of the in-game list even if marked read.

entries.title: Airship Departure Board
entries.pitch: CI/CD pipelines show as airship departures on a split-flap board at the landing or the FC workshop voyage console.
entries.how: A world-pinned panel at per-territory coordinates running a `gh run list --json` TUI loop; flip transition per cell in core/render.nelua. Workshop console found by EventObj DataId via a small GetObject extension and pinned like a target anchor.
entries.risks: Thin novelty over a pinned dashboard. Repo names leak in public spots and on stream, so add redaction. Hardcoded coordinates break on zone changes.

entries.title: Duty Complete Credits Roll
entries.pitch: Clearing a duty rolls Final Fantasy-style credits across your pet terminals, written from your session.
entries.how: Shim forwards IDutyState and IPartyList ClassJob ids; icons from ITextureProvider. lua/credits.lua builds text from Enter counts and CMD_END durations and feeds generated VT into a local session. Orbit via SetCameraState spring, gated on WatchingCutscene.
entries.risks: Must not cover the loot window or exit prompt. Default alias must not leak hostname. Duration stats need OSC 133.

entries.title: Eorzea Cron
entries.pitch: A crontab on Eorzea time and weather that rings your pet terminal for timed nodes and weather spawns.
entries.how: Host-side: ET = unix*3600/175, weather forecast from WeatherRate tables in a Lumina/Teamcraft dump, run by a systemd user timer. Notification writes BEL into the pet session; bell already bound. Optional amber pre-pulse via EVENT frame and a tint term in lighting().
entries.risks: WeatherRate tables change with patches. Island Sanctuary and Occult Crescent don't follow simple rules. GatherBuddy already has alarms; the draw is shell scripting.

entries.title: Git Status as Buffs and Debuffs
entries.pitch: Each pet terminal gets a mob-style nameplate with its branch and a buff row for repo state.
entries.how: precmd hook runs `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` with a timeout and emits a private OSC user var. Wire UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE in session.nelua to Lua on_uservar. worldview projects the nameplate above each pet via a world.nameplate(id) hook; click uses /term type.
entries.risks: Slow git in big repos adds prompt lag. Check whether OSC 1337 SetUserVar reaches the callback; else use an unused OSC number. Overlapping nameplates, stale state while asleep.

entries.title: Homecoming Boot Sequence
entries.pitch: Arriving home boots your installation screen by screen and marks what printed while you were away.
entries.how: Zone-gated anchors and agent replay already exist. Add on_zone_changed in Lua with staggered boot timers, per-session rez in worldview.nelua, an unread row mark in render.nelua set on sleep, and fold-out to one pet when no anchor matches. Per-house layouts need the housing location hook.
entries.risks: Amber marking fails for tmux and full-screen apps. Mostly presentation over existing persistence. Staggered boot needs a skip.

entries.title: Stream Redaction Mode
entries.pitch: Streamer mode seals password prompts and secret-looking text on every panel before it's drawn, with an optional Eorzean-script skin for looks.
entries.how: Agent checks tcgetattr after reads and sends SECRET_INPUT when ECHO is off with ICANON. lua/redact.lua regexes dirty rows (ghp_, AKIA, JWT, IPs, *_TOKEN=, key headers); render.nelua draws crystal quads over returned ranges on every surface including the first frame after wake. Cipher skin is a second font handle. Public flag persisted with layout.
entries.risks: ECHO signal fails inside tmux and ssh, leaving only regex; a missed pattern leaks. Masking must never lag a frame. No hold-to-peek, since OBS captures it. Fan font licensing.

entries.title: Parse Your Terminals
entries.pitch: A /term perf meter colors each terminal's frame cost like a DPS parse, and a governor tightens budgets inside duties.
entries.how: QueryPerformanceCounter around draw_terminal and world_transform_vertices, vertex deltas, byte counters per session. Governor caches flat panel geometry and on throttled frames skips render_state_update and render_termview, re-running only the transform. Shim forwards BoundByDuty, IsGPosing and local chat print.
entries.risks: Stale geometry cache after resize or font change draws garbage. Combat derez already cuts much of the duty cost. Chat notice should be opt-in.

entries.title: Pick the Winning Save
entries.pitch: When two machines changed the same save, show both side by side and let you choose, instead of renaming files by hand.
entries.how: resolve_conflicts already writes the conflicts table (live, kept_as, both mtimes) and names the loser 'name (older save, device ..., date).srm'. Expose unresolved rows through ArcadeSync.Conflicts in state.json with sizes and device names, add a 'swap <conflict id>' helper verb that exchanges the two names after a backup_saves call, and draw the pair in ArcadeWindow under the sync status.
entries.risks: Newer is not always better, which is the point, but players can still choose wrong; the swap must be reversible and itself recorded. Modification times differ across machines with bad clocks. Needs the sync path tested between two real machines, which has not happened yet.

entries.title: CRT Glass and Bezels
entries.pitch: Per-console scanline shaders and a cabinet bezel on the panel, chosen once and kept out of your own RetroArch settings.
entries.how: system_cfg_text already appends per-console overrides at launch without touching retroarch.cfg. Add video_shader_enable and a video_shader path, plus input_overlay for a bezel, from a per-console choice in config.json set by '/arcade look <console> <preset|off>'. The helper only points at shader presets already on disk (RetroArch's own slang shaders), and the window lists what it found.
entries.risks: Shaders cost GPU time inside the agent's headless compositor on top of FFXIV. Flatpak RetroArch sees only paths passed with --filesystem, so shader folders need adding to launch_argv. Standalone emulators are left out. Bezels shipped with the plugin would need their own licence check, so it starts with none.

entries.title: Crystal Pilgrimage
entries.pitch: Mark games finished and the Final Fantasy shelf gains a crystal for each one, a quiet record of working through the series.
entries.how: The 26-title shelf is already built from ArcadeShelfEntry and ArcadeGame.Ff keys. Add a finished flag with a date per game id, written by '/arcade finished <name>' and a button in the details strip, and kept in a small JSON file inside the synced tree so every machine agrees. CoverLayout draws the crystal mark on both picture and drawn covers; hours come from the play journal when present.
entries.risks: Marking is manual on purpose; reading emulator memory to detect an ending would be fragile and is not wanted. The synced file can conflict like any save and needs merge-by-union rules.

entries.title: /desktop doctor
entries.pitch: One command that walks every layer between the palette and a visible window, and says which one is broken, with evidence.
entries.how: A DoctorService in XivDesktop.Plugin runs the checks in order off the framework thread: CatalogService snapshot count and scan time, IpcContract.GhosttyCall/GhosttyPost HasAction, agent.status and focus.get through GhosttyCallBackend, then an opt-in launch of a harmless app and a wait for its request id to resolve in window.list's requests. Each step is a pure record in Core (step, evidence, verdict, fix) so the reasoning is host-testable; the result renders in a small ImGui window and can be copied as a redacted report for the issue template the README asks for.
entries.risks: It can only report what the IPC tells it; a mapped panel is still not proof the player can see it. The test launch starts a real program on the host, so it must be explicit and use something the player picks. The copied report must strip home paths, tokens and window titles.

entries.title: Let XivMcp Drive the Desk
entries.pitch: Ship the planned list_apps, launch_app, list_windows, window_action, switch_workspace and palette_search tools in XivMcp, on top of the XivDesktop.v1 gates that already exist.
entries.how: The gates are in src/Shared/IpcContract.cs (ListApps, Launch, Windows, Workspace, Palette, WindowAction) with parse helpers already. XivMcp registers thin tools that call them and return the JSON as is. Launch returns queued, not done, so launch_app should poll Windows for the new panel before reporting success.
entries.risks: A model that can launch apps can run programs on the host; launch_app needs a per-call confirmation or an allow list, the way the Claude permission dialog works. Tool results must say 'queued' honestly rather than 'opened'. Lives mostly in another repository.

entries.title: Channel Pull Timer
entries.pitch: A countdown anyone in a channel can start, drawn on every member's screen, without touching the game's own countdown.
entries.how: Channel messages are plain text today (LanternService.SendToChannel calls RoomSend with the string). Add a small structured envelope with a reserved prefix that carries a duration, not a clock time, parsed in XivLantern.Core and tested there. Command.Parse gains 'pull <seconds> [channel]'. The plugin draws an overlay window with no inputs and a toast through the existing INotificationManager at zero. It never sends /countdown or any game command.
entries.risks: Old clients show the envelope as a raw line, so the prefix must read sensibly as text. Relay latency makes timers drift by a few hundred milliseconds between members. People will ask for it to start the game's countdown; that is a game command and stays out.

entries.title: Show Me the Before and After
entries.pitch: The approval prompt for write_macro, equip_gearset and set_plugin_enabled shows what is there now next to what will be there, not only a sentence.
entries.how: Tools that already carry an approval sentence gain an optional preview callback: MacroWriteProvider reads the slot through MacroMemory, GearsetProvider reads the target set and get_equipment's current slots. The preview is rendered by ConfirmWindow and the Approvals tab (MainWindow.Approvals.cs) as a two-column table. It also lets McpServer.RenderApprovalSummary stop truncating write_macro at 500 characters, the open point in TODO.md. ToolContractTests gains a check that a preview never replaces the sentence.
entries.risks: The preview is taken when the prompt opens; the macro could change before approval, so the write must compare against the preview and fail if it moved. Reading macro and gear set memory needs the framework thread before the window draws. A long diff makes the prompt tall.

entries.title: Breadcrumbs Back
entries.pitch: Remember the way you came and point you back along it: /wayfinder back.
entries.how: Plugin.Update records your own position into a fixed ring buffer every couple of yalms (allocation-free, covered by AllocationBudgetTests), cleared on zone change. 'back' feeds the reversed crumbs to the existing PathFollow.NextCorner as if they were a vnavmesh path, and DrawTrail shows them. Nothing but your own character is recorded, and nothing is saved to disk.
entries.risks: Crumbs recorded while flying or swimming do not make a walkable path. Loops and backtracking need simplifying, or the bead leads you round every detour you made. Zone changes break the trail.

entries.title: Head to Head
entries.pitch: Pick two past benchmark runs and see them side by side, task by task, with the tool calls each model made.
entries.how: Every run is already in bench_runs with its full ResultJson (AlmanacStore.BenchRuns returns BenchRow). BenchmarkWindow's 'Past runs' header gets checkboxes and a Compare table built from the per-task entries in each result, with columns for tool validity, answer check and time to first token. Only runs with the same SuiteVersion are comparable; others are shown greyed with the reason.
entries.risks: Results from different context sizes, quantisations or mock versus live mode look comparable and are not, so the table must show those settings at the top. Old result JSON written before a schema change needs tolerant parsing.

entries.title: Context Gauge
entries.pitch: A small bar in the chat header that shows how full the model's context is, and trims old tool output before it overflows instead of after.
entries.how: ChatSession.Window cuts to the last 40 messages (HistoryWindow) whatever their size, so one large get_recipe result can fill a small context. ChatResult already carries PromptTokens; read the served context length from Ollama's /api/show or the gateway, store it per model next to model_caps, and replace the message-count window with a token budget that trims old tool output first, as the engine's [agent] context_tokens does. ChatWindow.DrawHeader draws the gauge.
entries.risks: Not every server reports prompt tokens or its context length, so the gauge needs an honest 'unknown' state and a character-count estimate. Trimming a tool result the model still needs makes it call the tool again or guess. Prompted mode puts the tool list in the system prompt, which counts too.

entries.title: Answers Back Over IPC
entries.pitch: A second IPC version that lets another plugin ask Almanac a question and receive the reply as it streams, not only open the chat window.
entries.how: Plugin.cs registers Almanac.ApiVersion (1) and Almanac.Ask (Func<string, bool>), which only opens ChatWindow and calls Send. Add ApiVersion 2 with Almanac.AskInThread returning a request id, and an Almanac.Event IPC message carrying the same events ChatSession.OnEvent already handles (TextDeltaEvent, ToolStartedEvent, ToolFinishedEvent, done or error), serialised like the engine's --stream-json lines. Requests run in their own ChatSession so they do not fight the window's thread.
entries.risks: Two ChatSessions against one local model double the load; requests need a queue and a busy answer. IPC messages are delivered on the caller's thread and a slow subscriber could stall streaming. Any plugin can call it, so it must not accept a system prompt or tool profile from the caller.

entries.title: Search Every Thread
entries.pitch: A search box over every conversation you have had with Almanac, so the answer from last Tuesday is two keystrokes away instead of lost in the sidebar.
entries.how: Add an FTS5 virtual table over messages.content in AlmanacStore's schema (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS beside threads/messages), kept in step by triggers so AppendMessage, ForkThread and DeleteThread need no changes. A new AlmanacStore.Search(query) returns (thread id, seq, snippet). ChatWindow.DrawThreads gets an input above 'New thread'; ChatSession.Open grows a seq to scroll to. Tool results are indexed but ranked below user and assistant lines.
entries.risks: FTS5 has to be present in the e_sqlite3 the plugin ships and loads inside Dalamud; SqliteNativeTests should assert it the way it asserts the version. The first open on an existing database has to backfill the index, which must not block the framework thread. Prompted-mode tool results are stored as user messages with PromptedTools.ResultPrefix and need filtering.

entries.title: Shelves of Your Own
entries.pitch: Make your own shelves, such as Backlog, Couch co-op or Comfort games, and put favourites at the top of the wall.
entries.how: ArcadeWindow already builds its Section list and CoverGrid per console. Add named shelves and favourites, keyed by the stable game_id, in a shelves file in the synced tree; the helper includes them in state.json and the window adds them as sections after the Final Fantasy shelf. Commands: '/arcade shelf <name> add|remove <game>' and a right-click menu on a cover. LaunchBox playlists could be read as starting shelves.
entries.risks: More shelves make Tab and L1/R1 navigation slower, so empty shelves should hide. game_id is title-based, so renaming a file to a different title drops it from its shelves.

entries.title: Covers from Your Own Screenshots
entries.pitch: Take a screenshot in the emulator and use it as that game's cover, a bring-your-own picture with no download involved.
entries.how: Point RetroArch's screenshot_directory at a per-console folder under the helper's data directory from system_cfg_text. A helper verb 'cover-from-shot <game>' copies the newest screenshot into the art tree as the game's own picture, ranked after the player's covers and before fetched ones in find_boxart. CoverLayout already fits pictures to each console's box aspect without stretching.
entries.risks: The games folder is never written to, so these must live outside it and not in covers/. Screenshots of wide or odd-resolution games crop badly; a crop preview may be needed. Standalone emulators use their own screenshot folders.

entries.title: Now Playing Widget
entries.pitch: An Umbra toolbar widget showing the running game and save-sync state, with one click to resume the last game.
entries.how: Follow the pattern ghostty-dalamud uses for its Umbra.Ghostty widget, without an assembly reference. ArcadeService.State already carries PlayingTitle, Sync.Code and the play history, so the widget reads them through a new XivArcade.v1.Status IPC call and launches through the existing XivArcade.v1.Launch.
entries.risks: Umbra's widget API changes between versions, and XivArcade must keep working with Umbra missing. The status call must be cheap, because toolbars poll often.

entries.title: Dresser and Armoire Tidy
entries.pitch: A read-only report of glamour items that could move to the Armoire, duplicates across dresser and bags, and sets that could be combined into outfits.
entries.how: A new tool in the Inventory providers joins the dresser contents GlamourProvider already reads with InventoryReader's containers and cached retainer inventories, then checks each item against the Cabinet sheet (Armoire-eligible) and the MirageStoreSetItem sheet (outfit sets) through IGameDataSource. It returns lists only; nothing is moved.
entries.risks: Dresser and retainer contents are only loaded after the player has opened them this session, so the answer must say which containers were not seen. Outfit rules around dyes and duplicates have edge cases. Pure planning, which is the point, but some will ask it to do the moving; it must not.

entries.title: Tool Call Inspector
entries.pitch: Click any grey tool line in the transcript to see the full arguments and result, how long it took, and whether the call passed schema validation.
entries.how: ChatSession.Shorten cuts tool lines to 120 characters and Render throws the rest away. Keep the StoredMessage seq on tool lines (it is already there), and on click load the full message from AlmanacStore.Messages, pretty-print it with System.Text.Json, and pair each call with its result by ToolCallId. Validation reasons come from Scorer.Validate as AgentLoop already records them in CallRecord. Rerun is only offered for tools in the read tier.
entries.risks: Tool results can be large, such as a full inventory, and drawing them every frame in ImGui is slow unless the text is cached and clipped. Prompted-mode threads store calls as plain assistant text, so pairing needs the PromptedTools parser. Rerunning an action-tier call must never be possible from here.

entries.title: Proper Icons on the Umbra Taskbar
entries.pitch: Show each open window's real app icon in the Umbra Windows widget instead of a letter tile.
entries.how: WindowsWidget.Item sets a LetterTile colour and letter today. Add an optional icon path to AppSummary and the Windows payload in IpcContract (additive, as the contract requires), filled from CatalogService's resolved PNG path, and let the widget load it through Una.Drawing's image style. Falls back to the letter tile when absent.
entries.risks: The Umbra layout and the reflection-based popup workaround are themselves unverified in game. Icon textures must be loaded once and shared, not per redraw. Depends on desk-svg-icons for full coverage.

entries.title: The Proving Ground
entries.pitch: A step-by-step window that walks you through the in-game checks in docs/WAYFINDER.md and builds a report to paste into an issue.
entries.how: A new window beside SettingsWindow, with the eight steps from 'Proving it in game' as data. Steps that can be checked automatically read WayfinderState (guide Walk, distance close to 20, source Flag, source Quest, Navmesh true, reason 'cutscene'); the others are manual ticks. The report joins WayfinderIpc.StatusLine, GloveTexture.Status and Navmesh.Status and goes to the clipboard, never the network.
entries.risks: An automatic tick proves only what the plugin believes, not what the player saw, so the report must keep the two kinds of evidence apart. The step list must stay in step with the doc.

entries.title: Folding Screen Splits
entries.pitch: Splitting a world terminal hinges it into a folding screen of panes you can angle, fold shut and walk around.
entries.how: Each leaf is its own Session; add group id and leaf index to layout persistence. Lua computes leaf placement from the group anchor with hinge yaw animated by spring(). No new projection math. Hinge drag is a new grip mode calling policy_world_hinge. Folded leaves sleep via sleep_unseen. /term split and fold commands.
entries.risks: Overlapping leaves need depth-sorted picking. Long-folded panes lose older scrollback on wake. Resizing a leaf must rebalance neighbours.

entries.title: News From the Lamplighter
entries.pitch: Each release posts its changelog entry to the author channel as a signed announcement, so players who opted in hear about fixes in game.
entries.how: tools/release.sh and tools/changelog.py already produce the player-facing entry from changelog.json. Add a step that signs it offline with the lantern CLI's author sign command (crates/lantern-cli/src/author.rs, which prints an ltannounce line with a growing --seq) and hands that line to the author node's /announce, per docs/AUTHOR.md. The plugin already verifies and shows announcements (LT_EV_ANNOUNCEMENT, AuthorChat).
entries.risks: AuthorIdentity.cs is still empty, so nothing can be verified until the author does the AUTHOR.md setup. Signing must stay on the author's machine and never move into CI. Too many announcements will get the channel muted.

entries.title: The Failing Suite (Extreme)
entries.pitch: Target a striking dummy and your test suite becomes a trial boss: failing tests are its HP, compiler errors pull as adds on an enemy list, and all green plays Duty Complete.
entries.how: A host wrapper runs the suite and the checker under watchexec, reads JUnit or JSON output (`cargo check --message-format=json`, `tsc --watch`, `ruff --output-format json`) and prints `ESC _ ffxiv;suite;pass=..;fail=..;fixed=..;top=<test> ESC \` plus `ffxiv;diag;<json>` snapshots, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE (session.nelua sets neither option today). A new lua/trial.lua diffs snapshots into damage, new adds and kills, ranks adds with primary errors first, and keeps a local hunt log. The hologram is a world panel on the existing `target` anchor raised above the dummy, running `less +G` on the top failure. Boss bar, enemy list and banner are ImGui in chrome.nelua's glass style; numbers go through a new shim call to IFlyTextGui.AddFlyText, and the nameplate is renamed in INamePlateGui.OnNamePlateUpdate only for a BattleNpc whose BNpcName is a striking dummy. Clicking an add writes `goto file:line` to the wrapper, which calls `nvim --server $NVIM --remote-send`.
entries.risks: Hitting the dummy puts you in combat, and combat derezzes everything, so this is a boss you watch, not one you fight. AddFlyText may only attach to your own character, so the dummy's numbers might have to be drawn by the plugin. One refactor can spawn 300 adds, so cap and roll them up, and crediting a root-cause fix with its cascade is a heuristic. Giant tracebacks carry paths and secrets. It's gated to dummies outside duties so it never looks like a real combat HUD.

entries.title: Your Feet Are the Mouse
entries.pitch: Lay a terminal flat on the floor and any mouse-aware TUI follows your character's footsteps as the pointer, with a jump as the click.
entries.how: place() already takes pitch, and world_axes and the depth-pass basis tilt with it, so a `floor` pin lays the panel flat at a Raycast ground height. Each frame ghostty.player() x/z is projected into panel pixels through that basis. The core builds a ghostty_mouse_encoder with setopt_from_terminal, so tracking (1000/1002/1003) and format (SGR 1006, SGR-pixels 1016) come from the app, plus OPT_SIZE and OPT_TRACK_LAST_CELL so motion reports only when you cross a cell. The shim adds ConditionFlag.Jumping to GuObject; its rising edge after a short dwell on a tile sends a button-1 press and release. Stepping on or off the board sends ghostty_focus_encode in or out when mode 1004 is set. Only your own character counts, and only in floor mode.
entries.risks: The plugin has never reported a click to a TUI (termview only encodes the wheel), so this is the mouse encoder's first user. Jumps are noisy, hence the dwell. Floors aren't flat everywhere, so raycast the corners and refuse slopes, and a flat panel may z-fight the floor in the depth test. Other players' positions must never become input.

entries.title: Algorave Conductor
entries.pitch: Live-code music in a terminal and your character conducts at the exact tempo, while the pattern that just played flares on the panel behind you.
entries.how: TidalCycles and Strudel's desktop setups send every event to SuperDirt as OSC over UDP. A host-side `ffxiv-tidal` reads a mirrored copy of that stream (orbit, cps, cycle, delta, sound) and prints `ffxiv;beat` APCs into a hidden session kept live with run_occluded, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. A new lua/conductor.lua converts cps to BPM and drives ghostty.anim_speed on a pose from animation.lua picked per tempo band, with anim_play flourishes on section changes, all client-side like the existing typing loop. For the flash it finds the row holding `d1 $` on the editor panel with ghostty_search_* and GHOSTTY_SEARCH_DATA_VIEWPORT_MATCHES, then glows that rect in the orbit's colour for the event's delta. Sonic Pi works the same way through its OSC cue log.
entries.risks: Poses played far off their normal speed look silly, so stick to tempo bands. Tidal doesn't report source spans, so matching an event to its line is a guess; Strudel's events do carry them. The UDP mirror must never add latency to SuperDirt. Animation changes are client-side but stay off in duties. Nobody in the venue sees the code unless they watch your stream.

entries.title: Cracktro Login
entries.pitch: Launching the game plays a 1990s cracktro over the title screen: a sine-scrolling greetz list, copper bars, a starfield and a MOD tune from your desk speakers.
entries.how: The intro is an ordinary terminal program on the agent host: `cracktro` draws truecolor half-block frames (kitty graphics once Kitty Graphics Tapestries lands) and plays the .mod with openmpt123. The core opens it at the title screen, when host.nelua reports not in world and IClientState.IsLoggedIn is false, as a borderless full-screen popup terminal. It holds render_state_update while DATA_MODE shows synchronized output (2026), so each frame presents whole. Greetz come from greetz.txt plus an FC name and friend names cached at your last logout (ClientStructs InfoProxyFriendList; fields to verify). Any key or pad button ends it with the existing derez, once per launch, skippable in settings.
entries.risks: Full-screen half-blocks at speed are heavy on the per-glyph ImDrawList path. render.nelua doesn't honour mode 2026 today. If the agent isn't reachable before login it must show nothing and never delay the menu. Friends' names on a streamed title screen are a leak, so friend greetz are opt-in. Copper bars need a calm preset, and MOD files carry their own licences.

entries.title: Cutscene Director
entries.pitch: Long commands finish like a story beat: letterbox bars, a camera move to the panel, and a Talk-style box reading the result.
entries.how: Shares the OSC 133 CMD_END frame with cast-bar-commands. Shim forwards BoundByDuty/WatchingCutscene/OccupiedInEvent and IToastGui. lua/director.lua sequences bars, camera (existing fly-in SetCameraState), box and return. Talk box is ImGui with game ULD textures, not the real AddonTalk.
entries.risks: Unprompted camera moves are jarring; abort on any input or condition change. Needs shell integration. Command names show on stream.

entries.title: Deploy as a Raid Pull
entries.pitch: CI jobs show as party frames, and a production deploy needs a charged Limit Break hold before Enter goes through.
entries.how: Capture session polls `gh run list/view --json` every ~10s to TSV; frames drawn with new ui.* progress widgets. ghostty.input_line(session) reads cursor-row cells with SEMANTIC_CONTENT==INPUT (OSC 133). keymap.lua swallows Enter on guarded patterns until the hold fills, then sends \r. Victory via anim_play, skipped while BoundByDuty.
entries.risks: A speed bump, not a safety control: needs OSC 133 and is bypassed from any other terminal. Swallowing Enter needs a visible reason and Esc to cancel. gh rate limits.

entries.title: Ready Checks for Your Agents
