entries.pitch: When an agent needs you mid-duty it waits for the wipe or the kill, and then every pending question arrives at once as a ready check.
entries.how: Claude Code's Notification and Stop hooks send `ghostty-emit waiting` (the EVENT frame from Your Agents Are a Light Party); other agents can use OSC 9 or 777, which reach GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION once session.nelua registers it. Out of combat the shim prints the line with IChatGui.Print and a link payload that focuses the session's panel; while InCombat or BoundByDuty is set, lines queue. The Ready Check opens on ICondition.ConditionChange (combat off) or IDutyState.DutyWiped and DutyCompleted, as a local window styled after the game's, never the real /readycheck. Each row renders the session's bottom rows from render state, options are parsed from lines shaped like `1. Yes`, and a click sends only that digit through the key encoder to that session. CLAUDE.md can also tell agents to call an in-game MCP server's duty-state tool before asking and keep working while you're inside.
entries.risks: One-click approvals between pulls is how you approve an `rm -rf` without reading it, so rows show the full command and destructive patterns can't be answered from the check. Parsing Claude Code's prompt off the screen breaks when its TUI changes. Local lines must never look like a real player's tell, both for clarity and honest screenshots. Nothing is ever sent to other players.

entries.title: Feed It to the Familiar
entries.pitch: Alt-drag a failing terminal onto your AI companion and it swallows the last command's output as context and starts on the fix.
entries.how: world.drop(id, pose) already fires when an Alt-drag ends (core/policy.nelua:544); lua/world.lua checks the drop point against panels whose profile has `familiar = true`. The core scans GHOSTTY_ROW_DATA_SEMANTIC_PROMPT upward for the last OSC 133 prompt, takes a grid ref on the output after it, calls ghostty_terminal_select_output and ghostty_terminal_selection_format_alloc (plain, unwrapped, trimmed, capped to the tail). A header adds DATA_TITLE, DATA_PWD from OSC 7, the command from INPUT-semantic cells and the exit code from the agent's CMD_END frame. The block goes through ghostty_paste_encode into the familiar's session as a bracketed paste. Without OSC 133 it falls back to a PLAIN formatter over the viewport. The swallow reuses the present and fly-in tween in worldview.nelua.
entries.risks: It sends terminal output, env dumps and tokens in stderr included, to a hosted model: show a byte count, redact token-shaped strings, confirm the first time. If the familiar sits in a permission prompt the paste lands in the wrong place, so drops are refused unless its last hook state is idle. The source shell needs OSC 133 through tmux and ssh. Alt-drag already means move, so drop targets need a clear highlight.

entries.title: Fishing for Errors
entries.pitch: Each new kind of error on your machines becomes a fish in the pond, and when you land a real catch it leaps out as a glowing hologram and goes into your Error Guide.
entries.how: On the agent host, `xiv-pond` tails journalctl and app logs, collapses lines into signatures by stripping numbers, hex and paths (drain3-style templates), and writes `ESC _ ffxiv;fish;<sig>;<severity>;<count>;<text> ESC \` into a hidden session kept live with run_occluded. The core captures these through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE and queues them. The shim adds a read of ConditionFlag.Fishing and an IChatGui.ChatMessage filter for your own catch message, and only after that message does Lua pop the most severe queued error. Its leap arc starts at a Raycast point ahead of your facing; severity and count set size and colour. The Error Guide is a ghostty.ui tab saved beside world-state.lua; double-click an entry to open its log on a panel.
entries.risks: It must never signal bites, hook timing or anything else about the real fish, which would be fishing assistance; it reacts only after the game has told you what you caught. Catch messages differ by client language. Bad templates turn one bug into a hundred species. Log lines carry tokens and hostnames, so redact on the host. It's flavour, not monitoring, so keep a real alert alongside it.

entries.title: Allagan Terminal Scenes
entries.pitch: RP hosts and venues run hackable in-world consoles backed by sandboxed scripts that invited players walk up to and use.
entries.how: World anchor shared in the invite. Agent guest tokens with a forced command, like ssh ForceCommand: ATTACH only to the scene session, which runs in a container or restricted user. Client line-buffers and tags lines with name@world. Restricted session mode ignores OSC 52, notifications and hyperlinks. Theme palette plus a licensed fan font via the font atlas. Venue discovery by opt-in directory keyed on ward/plot is research.
entries.risks: Guests on a host is the core security problem: sandbox mandatory, rate caps, relay to hide IPs. Content sits outside SE moderation. Tiny audience, and non-plugin players see people typing at thin air.

entries.title: Loot-Roll Job Results
entries.pitch: Jobs that finish mid-fight wait for combat to end, then drop at your feet as coffers you triage with Need, Greed or Pass.
entries.how: `term notify` asks the agent via a control socket to OPEN a detached session; a PROTO_EVENT frame reports completion. Nelua queues while in_combat and releases after ~5s out. Lua 'drop' anchor springs at your feet tinted by status. Need=ATTACH+make_pet, Greed=OPEN same argv, Pass=CLOSE via existing gesture code.
entries.risks: Combat flag flickers on trains; debounce. Skip bindings while the game's NeedGreed addon is open. Greed re-running a deploy needs confirmation. ssh-launched jobs need the socket forwarded.

entries.title: Moogle Mail
entries.pitch: When a background job, ssh session or tmux alert finishes, a delivery moogle only you can see hands you the result as a letter.
entries.how: Triggers: agent EXIT for detached sessions, OSC 9/777 and bell callbacks, plus an agent-side NOTIFY frame so sleeping sessions don't miss completions. mail.lua queues letters (id, title, last N lines), holds them until out of combat and duty, and persists with layout. Parchment theme in render.nelua; letter opens as a pet via place_pet. v1 moogle: ImGui billboard from a game icon texture on pet springs; optional local IChatGui.Print with a link payload. v2: client-side moogle actor (weeks, research).
entries.risks: Client-side actors crash on zoning and must never spawn in duties or cutscenes. Sprite draws through walls. Needs shell integration or wrappers. Stderr on screen can leak secrets on stream. Share one pipeline with the visual bell and taskbar.

entries.title: Ops Weather
entries.pitch: Server health sets your local weather, client-side, so you feel an outage before you read about it.
entries.how: Agent probe runner sends status over a new EVENT frame. New ops.lua maps states to per-territory weather ids with hysteresis. Shim adds SetWeatherOverride/ClearWeatherOverride beside GetEnvironment using the client-side WeatherManager path Brio and Weatherman use. M.lighting() already reads weather and rain, so tint and backlight follow for free; rain beads drawn in worldview.nelua.
entries.risks: Not every weather id is valid per territory; houses and duties have none or script their own. Hides real weather from fishers and gatherers, so it needs a toggle and guaranteed restore on unload, zone change and duty. Fights Brio or Weatherman.

entries.title: Over-the-Shoulder Pets
entries.pitch: Friends who opt in make their orbiting pet terminal visible to you as a live read-only screen.
entries.how: Read-only guest tokens scoped to one session plus a PAUSE frame on minimize; LIST already reports attached count. A second AgentClient per share with sessions flagged read-only. Invite carries name@world, matched against target/object table. Generalize the pet anchor to any entity_id.
entries.risks: Screens may show secrets; needs a clear broadcasting indicator. Skip or clear the 256 KiB replay for guests. Pet positions won't line up exactly across clients.

entries.title: Tomestones for Dead Shells
entries.pitch: When a process dies its panel falls and leaves a tomestone on the spot, holding an exact snapshot of its last screen and scrollback.
entries.how: On PROTO_EXIT, Session:mark_exited calls ghostty_snapshot_encode_alloc and writes a GHOSTSNP file beside world-state.lua with territory, pose, argv, cwd (DATA_PWD from OSC 7), title (DATA_TITLE), runtime and status; the agent already reports signals as 128+N. The panel derezzes into a drawn slab with the epitaph. Opening a stone builds a transport-less, read-only Session: ghostty_snapshot_decoder_new_buf, decode to decoder_ready so the final screen draws at once, then decoder_next brings older scrollback in as you scroll. A sleeping panel is detached and never sees EXIT, and the agent drops exited sessions, so the agent must hold a finished session until a client collects it, or link libghostty-vt itself (tools/build.sh already builds the host library) and snapshot at the moment of death. `/tome` is already an alias of `/term`, so `raise` is just a new subcommand.
entries.risks: Snapshots keep every secret that was on screen: per-profile opt-out, a retention cap and make_private file permissions. vt.h warns the API will change, so version the files and treat old ones as best effort. A graveyard of every `ls` would be silly, so only long runs or non-zero deaths get a stone.

entries.title: Static War Room
entries.pitch: Your static or FC gets one read-only strat board pinned at the same arena wall or FC house spot on every member's client.
entries.how: World anchors are identical across instances; share as a save_state snippet restored when zone matches (FC house needs HousingManager id). Members attach with read-only guest tokens to a separate broadcast agent; one PTY means scroll sync is free. Shim forwards IDutyState start/wipe/complete; only the lead writes pull number and time. Leader ping is an EVENT frame that turns pets and highlights rows.
entries.risks: Never parse combat events or show timelines, which would make it a trigger tool. Lead's agent dropping kills everyone's board. Discord screen share covers the basics. Needs opacity for sightlines.

entries.title: Wardrobe by Hostname
entries.pitch: Glamourer IPC dresses you for the machine you're on, so prod looks different from dev.
entries.how: OSC 7 PWD_CHANGED and title give the host; forward on_host(id, host) to Lua. lua/wardrobe.lua maps globs to Glamourer designs for the focused session with ~1s debounce. Shim adds typed forwards for Glamourer apply/revert with a lock key. Sudo from a prompt regex on the cursor row.
entries.risks: Plain ssh without OSC 7 or titles gives nothing. Glamourer automation can fight the state; crash mid-apply leaves the outfit on. IPC signatures change, so pin the API version.

entries.title: Duty Pop Pause
entries.pitch: When the Duty Finder pops, your arcade game saves a state and pauses, and it offers to resume when you are back.
entries.how: Add network_cmd_enable and a fixed network_cmd_port to system_cfg_text in tools/xiv-arcade, so every RetroArch launch accepts local UDP commands. PadCaptureService already watches ICondition for combat and cutscenes; add a DutyPop reason to the PadRelease enum, raised from ConditionFlag.WaitingForDuty or an IAddonLifecycle PostSetup on ContentsFinderConfirm. On it, ArcadeService asks the helper (new 'pause' verb) to send SAVE_STATE then PAUSE_TOGGLE, checked with GET_STATUS first so a paused game is not unpaused. On leaving the duty, the resume offer is a chat link, never automatic.
entries.risks: It must only watch the pop, never click Commence; that line is absolute. PAUSE_TOGGLE is a toggle, so a lost reply can leave the game running. Standalone PCSX2 and DuckStation have no equivalent command channel, so they get the pad release only. The UDP port is open on localhost to anything on the machine. None of the underlying pad or panel path has been seen in game yet.

entries.title: A Linkshell for Your Agents
entries.pitch: A private in-game channel where agents post short messages in their own colour and you reply with a slash command, delivered to them as a resource update.
entries.how: print_echo already writes [MCP]-tagged lines to the player's own log only. Give each client a stable colour and prefix, and add `/xivmcp say <agent> <text>` in the command handler Plugin.cs registers; messages go to a bounded per-client inbox exposed as ffxiv://inbox with notifications/resources/updated through NotifierProxy, plus a read_inbox tool. The EventStream gains a 'message' kind so get_events clients see it too.
entries.risks: Echo lines are the player's own log, but they still sit in chat logs that other plugins read and export, so secrets posted by an agent end up there. Clients must subscribe to resources for replies to feel live. A /say typo such as '/say claude' would post in public Say chat, so the command name must be hard to confuse.

entries.title: Your Unfinished Sightseeing Log, as Objectives
entries.pitch: A tool that reads which vistas you have not logged and posts each as a custom objective with its spot, emote, Eorzea time and weather window.
entries.how: A static provider reads the Adventure sheet through IGameDataSource (so the standalone host can answer the data half) for the Level location, emote and time columns; a live half checks completion through ClientStructs' PlayerState adventure flags via ILiveWorld. The result feeds ObjectiveFactory directly, and the time and weather become the objective's eorzeaTime and weather conditions that ObjectiveEvaluator and find_weather_windows already compute.
entries.risks: Which Adventure columns carry the weather requirement must be checked against Lumina and may need a small hand-kept table for some entries. The completion flags are unverified in game like every ClientStructs read here. Posting a whole expansion's log at once hits the 200-objective cap, so it works a region at a time.

entries.title: Where Is the Mender?
entries.pitch: Point at an NPC by name, /wayfinder find mender, using where the game's own data places them.
entries.how: Build an index once from the Level sheet rows whose Type is an ENpc, joined to ENpcResident for names and titles ('Mender' is usually a title). Match with ZoneMatch's exact, then prefix, then substring ranking over ZoneMatch.Fold. Among placements pick the nearest in your zone first, like QuestPick.Nearest, else fall back to the aetheryte hint. Results become an Explicit Target with the NPC's name as the label, Y included so vnavmesh gets a proper floor.
entries.risks: Many NPCs have several Level rows or appear only during certain quest phases, so the game data can place someone who is not there. Generic titles match dozens of NPCs. Building the index costs a noticeable moment on first use and must happen off the framework thread.

entries.title: Treasure Hunt Routes
entries.pitch: Build a route of stops with a riddle at each and share it as a pasteable code, so an FC can run a scavenger hunt with nothing but chat.
entries.how: A route is a small JSON list of (territory, x, z, label, clue, hidden) compressed and base64-encoded with a version prefix; parsing and validation go in Core using WayfinderIpc.Validate and CleanLabel for every stop, so a malicious code can do nothing but point. Builds on way-waypoint-queue. 'Hidden' stops show no bead until the previous one is reached, only the clue in DrawNote. Recording a route is /wayfinder route add at each spot. No network: the code is passed by hand.
entries.risks: Codes get long for many stops and chat limits message length. Hidden stops can be cheated by reading the code, which is fine for fun and should be said plainly. Clues are player-written text, so they need the same cleaning labels get.

entries.title: Answers You Can Click
entries.pitch: Map coordinates, item names and duty names in a reply become small buttons that place the flag or show the details, without asking the model again.
entries.how: Structured tool results (ToolOutcome.Json, kept in CallRecord) already name the zones, items and coordinates the answer was built from, so matching the reply against those is more reliable than parsing free text. ChatWindow's LineKind.Assistant branch renders spans instead of one TextUnformatted. Clicks call engine.XivMcpToolsAsync() then McpToolSource.CallAsync("set_map_flag" | "get_item" | "find_owned_items") directly, going through XivMcp's normal tiers.
entries.risks: Wrapped ImGui text with inline buttons is fiddly and costs frame time on long transcripts. A model that invents coordinates would get a flag in the wrong place, so only values that came out of a tool result become links. Old threads reopened from SQLite have lost the in-memory CallRecords unless tool JSON is re-parsed from the stored messages.

entries.title: Spoiler Guard
entries.pitch: Almanac checks how far you are in the main scenario and keeps its answers about lore, NPCs and later zones behind that line unless you ask it not to.
entries.how: At the start of a thread, and when the zone changes, call XivMcp's get_quest_status for a short list of main scenario milestones and put the furthest completed one into the system prompt that ChatSession builds each turn, with a rule not to reveal later events. A toggle in settings and a /almanac spoilers on|off subcommand in Plugin.OnCommand. Answers based on search_quests or get_quest for quests beyond that point get a warning line.
entries.risks: A local model's own training is the main source of spoilers and a prompt rule will not stop all of them; this lowers the risk and must say so. Choosing the milestone list takes knowledge of the story and upkeep every patch. Players on a new character may have finished the story on another.

entries.title: Flow-State Limit Break
entries.pitch: Typing fast fills a client-side Limit Break gauge that fires a flourish at your peak.
entries.how: Extend animation.lua typing energy with a rolling WPM window and three segments; ImGui gauge; payoff via anim_play of a job LB timeline the pose guard allows. Aura needs an actor VFX forward. Finger IK toward the Model M is dropped.
entries.risks: LB timelines are job-specific, some long and camera-bound. Rewards typing garbage into a shell. Aura VFX is stretch.

entries.title: Mount to Furnishing
entries.pitch: Pin terminals to real housing items, so a painting or bookshelf becomes a screen that moves with the furniture.
entries.how: Shim forwards HousingManager location (house/ward/plot/room) and IndoorTerritory furniture (item id, transform), as MakePlace and BDTH read. New 'furniture' anchor in lua/world.lua matched by item id plus nearest transform, followed every frame, with per-item offset/size from a hand-made table. Replaces zone check with house-id check, since same-size houses share a territory id.
entries.risks: Panels show through walls and floors without depth; gate by room or height. Structs change with patches and load async. Identical adjacent items confuse matching. Frame fitting needs manual calibration.

entries.title: Legible at 40 Yalms
entries.pitch: Distance LOD for world panels: full text up close, block minimap rows mid-range, a one-line nameplate far away.
entries.how: draw_world already has projected corners; divide by rows for on-screen cell height and pick glyphs, run blocks (reuse the merged background-run loop), or nameplate from title, last row or OSC 9;4 progress. Lua owns thresholds with hysteresis. Font mip handles at 20/40/80px chosen in PushWorldFont. MSDF is research.
entries.risks: No ligatures: per-cell AddText, no shaper. Big font atlases grow fast. LOD pop needs cross-fade.

entries.title: Queue Pop Eject
entries.pitch: When the Duty Finder pops, whatever terminal owns your screen lets go, and an opt-in hook lets your desk react.
entries.how: Shim forwards IClientState.CfPop duty id via gu_event. Nelua clears world_full_id and stops capturing keyboard. Lua on_duty_pop picks pet or minimize and sets a countdown title cleared on WaitingForDutyFinder/BoundByDuty. Client-to-agent EVENT frame fork/execs an opt-in hook with only DUTY_ID in env.
entries.risks: Focus not released means you can't press Commence; test hardest. CfPop may miss some queue types. Never auto-commit, never type into the PTY.

entries.title: Soul Crystal Themes
entries.pitch: Terminal palettes re-derive live from your job, HUD theme and chat colors, and the prompt can show the real job icon.
entries.how: Set GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_COLOR_PALETTE with a per-frame lerp; lua/theme.lua builds 16 colors with a contrast clamp while app OSC overrides still win. Shim forwards ClassJob, ClassJobChanged and IGameConfig HUD/chat colors. Job icon drawn as a texture at a placeholder codepoint; prompt queries job via custom OSC.
entries.risks: SeIconChar shares the PUA with Nerd Font powerline glyphs and ImWchar is 16-bit, hence textures. Job colors have poor contrast without clamping. Config option names need checking.

entries.title: Handheld Bridge
entries.pitch: Setup profiles that make a Steam Deck or an Android RetroArch share the same synced save tree, so you can continue on the sofa.
entries.how: The synced tree is already device-neutral: game_id is a hash of system and title, and system_cfg_text turns off per-core sorting. Add 'xiv-arcade sync-setup --profile deck|android' that prints the matching RetroArch overrides for that device (savefile_directory, savestate_directory, the sort flags) and the Syncthing folder path, like syncthing_folder_commands does today. The plugin shows it as an extra step in the first-run list.
entries.risks: Android scoped storage and Syncthing forks make folder paths awkward. EmuDeck and similar setups sort saves per core and may overwrite the overrides. The handheld has no settle gate, so a game started there while saves arrive can still create a conflict.

entries.title: Save State Snapshots
entries.pitch: See your save states as screenshots in the details strip and start a game straight into the one you pick.
entries.how: Turn on savestate_thumbnail_enable in system_cfg_text so RetroArch writes a PNG beside each state in states/<console>/, which already syncs. The helper lists states per game into state.json; ArcadeWindow loads the PNGs through the same background CoverCache thumbnails used for covers. A launch takes an optional slot and launch_argv passes RetroArch's entry-slot option.
entries.risks: The entry-slot flag needs a recent RetroArch and must be checked against the Flatpak version before relying on it. State files are core-specific, so a state from Snes9x will not load in bsnes; show the core with each frame. PCSX2 and DuckStation keep states in their own formats and come later.

entries.title: Controller Ring Launcher
entries.pitch: A radial app ring on the gamepad for Steam Deck and couch players, with favourites on the sticks and workspaces on the shoulder buttons.
entries.how: Read IGamepadState in KeybindService alongside IKeyState and feed a pad chord into ChordTracker. The ring is a new ImGui window drawing UserLists favourites with IconDrawer; stick angle picks a sector. Launch and workspace steps go through CommandRunner, so nothing new reaches Ghostty.
entries.risks: Any button combo the ring uses is also read by the game; it must be a chord the player chooses and ideally one the game leaves unbound. Panel apps still want a keyboard, so this launches and arranges, it does not make a browser controller-friendly.

entries.title: Glamour Plates for Your Desk
entries.pitch: Save a named set of apps and placements, and put the whole arrangement on with one palette entry.
entries.how: A Layout record in Core (app id, workspace, pin args, order) with a pure planner that diffs it against the current window list, the way WorkspaceModel.Plan already diffs visibility. Applying launches missing apps through window.open, waits for request ids to resolve in window.list's requests, then issues window.place and the workspace moves. Saved in Configuration beside Workspaces; exposed as palette rows and an additive XivDesktop.v1 gate.
entries.risks: Windows appear asynchronously and some apps open several windows or a splash first, so matching window to app is fuzzy (WindowApps helps). Placement arguments are relative to the character, so the same plate lands differently in different spots. Launching six apps at once is slow.

entries.title: The Desk Knows Where You Are
entries.pitch: Bind a layout or workspace to a territory, so your house, the inn and Limsa each get their own arrangement back when you arrive.
entries.how: Subscribe to IClientState.TerritoryChanged in SessionService (AskService already does). A small Core map from territory id, and for housing the ward and plot where the client state exposes it, to a plate name or workspace number. On change, run the same layout planner as named plates. The Configuration gains a per-territory table; ARCHITECTURE.md already lists this as planned.
entries.risks: Zone changes happen while panels are mid-request; everything must wait until the load finishes. Housing identifiers are less stable than territory ids across patches. Instanced areas share a territory, so the match may be coarser than the player expects.

entries.title: An Agent May Ask You One Question
entries.pitch: A Ui tool that puts a short multiple-choice question on your screen and hands the answer back, so an agent stops guessing which gear set or which retainer you meant.
entries.how: A new ask_player tool (Ui tier, marked RequiresApproval=false as it only displays to the owner, listed in ToolContractTests' display-only set) takes a question and two to five choices, returns a question id at once and exposes ffxiv://questions/{id} with notifications/resources/updated on the answer, the same shape as tickets. The window reuses ConfirmWindow's layout and the pull-safe hold for combat. MCP's own elicitation/create is a later option once clients render it; McpServer.Dispatch has no handler for it today.
entries.risks: A chatty agent could ask twenty questions an hour; it needs a per-client cap and a 'stop asking' button. Answers are free text to the model, so choices must stay short labels, never a way to route the player into a gated action without its own prompt. Clients that do not subscribe to resources must poll.

entries.title: Station Modes
entries.pitch: Pick a station's mode (My Station, Crowd Faves, Deep Cuts, Discovery, Newly Released, Artist Only) where Pandora offers them to your account.
entries.how: pianobar asks for modes with interactiveradio.v1.getAvailableModesSimple (stationId) and sets one with interactiveradio.v1.setAndGetAvailableModes (stationId, modeId), through the same JSON API and Blowfish wrapping PandoraClient.CallAsync already does. A mode picker beside the station name in MainWindow.DrawNowPlaying; a mode change clears Radio's queue so the next song follows it.
entries.risks: These calls are newer than the rest and less documented; whether they answer for the Android and Pandora One partners XivPiano signs in as, and for free accounts, has to be found out first. Pandora offers different modes per station, so the picker must list only what the answer says.

entries.title: The Next Aether Current
entries.pitch: Point at the nearest aether current in this zone that you have not yet attuned to.
entries.how: The AetherCurrentCompFlgSet sheet lists each zone's currents; field currents are EObj placements found through Level rows. FFXIVClientStructs' PlayerState reports which currents are unlocked. A new source (or a queue fed into way-waypoint-queue) keeps the nearest unattuned one as the target, re-read at the same 0.25 s scan Plugin.Update already does for the flag and quest.
entries.risks: Quest-rewarded currents have no field position and must be named, not pointed at. Plugins that already do this exist; this would need to be clearly nicer, not merely present. The EObj-to-current mapping has to be checked in game.

entries.title: Pointing on the Wing
entries.pitch: When you are mounted and flying, ask vnavmesh for a flight path and let the bead climb and dive with it.
entries.how: Navmesh.Request always passes fly = false to vnavmesh.Nav.PathfindCancelable. Pass true when ICondition shows InFlight (and Diving under water), and requery on take-off and landing through PathFollow.ShouldRequery. Heading.Ahead gains a pitched variant so the bead follows the path's height; the glove stays a ground-plane pointer with an up or down hint.
entries.risks: vnavmesh's flight meshes are less tested than its ground meshes. A flying path to a flag without height has no obvious end altitude. Must stay pointing only: never vnavmesh's movement gates, in the air as on the ground.

entries.title: The Quest Continues Next Door
entries.pitch: When a quest step lies on another map, point at the exit the game's own quest link names instead of just saying 'another zone'.
entries.how: docs/WAYFINDER.md lists AgentMap.MapQuestLinkContainer (QuestId, LevelId, source and target map) as 'not used yet'. GameReader.Quest reads it when no marker or to-do Level is in the player's zone and returns the link's Level as the target, labelled with the destination. Core gains a pure chooser beside QuestPick.Nearest, host-tested.
entries.risks: The container reflects what the map has loaded, the same known gap the event markers have. Links can point at places the player can only reach by ferry or NPC. Needs checking against a real journal, which nothing in the quest reads has had yet.

entries.title: Context Fit Finder
entries.pitch: A wizard step that tries the chosen model at 8k, 16k and 32k context, measures VRAM and speed at each, and recommends the largest that does not spill into system RAM.
entries.how: SetupWindow already computes the VRAM budget (GpuInfo, GameReserveMb) and Engine.BenchRunnerAsync builds a runner with an IVramProbe (OllamaVramProbe first, NvidiaSmiProbe as fallback) sampled by VramSampler. Run a three-task subset of Suite.Bundled() with Ollama's num_ctx option per step, record peak VRAM and tok/s, and detect spill as a sharp drop in speed or Ollama reporting size_vram below size.
entries.risks: Only Ollama takes a per-request context size; LM Studio and llama.cpp fix it at load time, so for them this can only advise. Each step reloads the model, which takes time and briefly competes with the game for VRAM. Under Wine, nvidia-smi may not be reachable from inside the game.

entries.title: Give the VRAM Back for Duties
entries.pitch: When the model shares the game's GPU, unload it as you enter a duty and load it again when you leave, so savage frame rates do not pay for an idle chatbot.
entries.how: Only when AlmanacSettings.GameOnSameGpu is set. For an Ollama backend (BackendKind), POST /api/generate with keep_alive 0 on BoundByDuty and a no-prompt load with keep_alive -1 on leaving, the same calls the engine's residency loop makes. The ServerDetector root URL and Engine.Quick HttpClient already exist for this. Skip it while ChatSession is Busy, and show the state in the chat header.
entries.risks: With the Almanac gateway as the engine, its own residency loop pins the model while ffxiv_dx11.exe runs and will fight the plugin, so the gateway needs a way to be told, or the plugin must stay out of it. LM Studio and llama.cpp have no equivalent API. Reloading a model right as the duty ends causes a stutter in town; a delay helps.

entries.title: Headroom Gauge
entries.pitch: A live readout of VRAM used by the game and the model, and of the last reply's tokens per second, so you can see a hub or a busy FATE pushing the model out.
entries.how: Reuse IVramProbe from Bench/Vram.cs on a slow timer (every few seconds, off the framework thread), plus DXGI's QueryVideoMemoryInfo next to the adapter enumeration in GpuInfo.cs for the game's own budget. Tokens per second come from ChatResult's OutputTokens and elapsed time, already measured for the benchmark. ChatWindow.DrawHeader shows it; thresholds come from GameReserveMb.
entries.risks: QueryVideoMemoryInfo through DXVK under Wine may report numbers that do not match the real card. nvidia-smi polling costs a process spawn each time; keep it slow or use the Ollama probe. Numbers that jump about will worry people more than help them, so smoothing matters.

entries.title: Your Own Notes as a Tool
entries.pitch: Point Almanac at a folder of Markdown notes, such as your glamour plans, retainer ventures or static's strats, and the model can search them in game.
entries.how: A NotesToolSource implementing IToolSource with two read-only tools, notes_search and notes_read, backed by an FTS5 index in almanac.sqlite (the Python engine's knowledge base does the same with SQLite FTS5, so its front-matter format can be reused). Engine.NewLoop adds it to the ToolHub list; ToolProfiles gains the two names in SmallSet so small models see it. Re-index on a file-change watcher or on a Refresh button in SettingsWindow.
entries.risks: Notes go to whatever model server is configured, which may not be local; the settings page has to say that. A large folder makes results long and eats a small context (see the context gauge). A file watcher under Wine on a Z: path may not fire, so manual refresh has to exist anyway.

entries.title: Inherits Your Accessibility Settings
entries.pitch: The terminal follows the game's color-blindness filter, supports accessible fonts per tab, and can speak matching output lines.
entries.how: CVD-safe palette preset chosen from a forwarded IGameConfig color-filter option. Per-profile font handles via AddFontFromFile. Agent strips escapes, regex-matches lines and sends a small frame; speech via host-side piper/espeak, SAPI or TextToTalk IPC as options.
entries.risks: No global high-contrast mode to inherit; offer a manual AAA palette. SAPI under Wine is poor, so prefer host TTS. Rate-limit speech so it never talks over callouts.

entries.title: Gaze and Presence
entries.pitch: Your character turns to the focused panel, startles when a background terminal rings, and dozes after long idle.
entries.how: Body turn exists (rate-limited set_rotation); trigger on focus change. Bell already bound in ghostty.nelua; emit on_bell to Lua for a startle timeline, turn and backlight pulse. Doze is an idle timer in animation.lua. Head look-at is research and deferred.
entries.risks: Merge with the in-progress visual bell rather than building twice. Only rotate while stationary. Look-at conflicts with posing plugins.

entries.title: Hover-to-Shell Market Board
entries.pitch: Hovered items stream into your shell, so a Universalis CLI draws cross-world price history beside the retainer bell.
entries.how: Shim forwards IGameGui.HoveredItemChanged and home DC via gu_event; Nelua debounces ~150ms and relays PROTO_EVENT. `term events --kind hover` feeds a shell script calling Universalis. Panel shown while OccupiedSummoningBell.
entries.risks: Not every row raises a tooltip. Universalis is crowd-sourced and rate-limited. Existing plugins already show prices; the draw is your own tooling. Never write prices back.

entries.title: Live Cross Hotbar Shell Slots
entries.pitch: Hotbar slots bound to shell jobs show live progress rings, so a Steam Deck player can watch a build without opening a terminal.
entries.how: Shim forwards _ActionCross/_ActionBar slot rects plus RaptureHotbarModule and macro text. Nelua maps `/term focus <name>` slots (needs named sessions) and draws rings on the foreground list. `term slot` arrives as PROTO_EVENT. Hold detection from GamepadDown plus active set.
entries.risks: HUD layouts, WXHB and scale plugins break slot rects. Macro fires on press before hold. Niche for the effort.

entries.title: Open With, from inside the game
entries.pitch: Pick a file in an in-game file dialog and open it in the right host app, using the %f and %u codes the Exec parser already knows about.
entries.how: ExecLine.StripFieldCodes currently expands %f %F %u %U to nothing; add a variant that substitutes one or many shell-quoted Linux paths. DesktopEntryParser keeps MimeType; AppCatalog builds a mime index. The picker is Dalamud's FileDialogManager over Z:\, and HostPaths maps the chosen Wine path back to the Linux path before it goes to window.open. A new PaletteCommand kind 'open' and a right-click 'Open file with…' in LauncherWindow.
entries.risks: Mime detection needs a guess from the extension or the agent running xdg-mime; Wine cannot see everything the host can. Flatpak apps need their --file-forwarding markers kept rather than dropped. Paths with odd characters are exactly where quoting bugs hide, so this needs fuzz tests beside FuzzTests.

entries.title: Up For It Tags
entries.pitch: Tick a few typed tags (maps, roulettes, crafting, ex, chat) and friends can filter the list to people who want the same thing tonight.
entries.how: Extend Wire::Heartbeat in crates/lantern-core/src/node/friends.rs with a tags field, or better add a new Heartbeat2 variant at the end of the enum so old nodes keep decoding, and store tags beside status/note for each friend device. Surface them in lt_friend_list JSON, FriendView and GetFriends over IPC. MainWindow.DrawList gains a filter chip row. Tags are chosen from a fixed list plus free text the player types; nothing comes from the game.
entries.risks: A wire change needs a compatibility plan: postcard enums break if variants are reordered, and mixed versions will run side by side for weeks. Free-text tags need the same clamping and ChatText.Clean treatment as notes. Tempting to auto-fill from the duty finder, which the design forbids.

entries.title: Pass a Picture Along
entries.pitch: Share a screenshot or small file with a friend or channel, peer to peer, shown as a thumbnail you choose to open.
entries.how: The network half exists: lt_blob_add_file, lt_blob_offer, lt_blob_fetch and LT_EV_BLOB_OFFER/PROGRESS/DONE are in lantern.h and wrapped by LanternNode.BlobAddFile/BlobOffer/BlobFetch. The plugin needs a picker (a path field or drag from the file system), an offer line in ChatBook, fetch on click into a folder under the plugin config directory, and a thumbnail through ITextureProvider for PNG and JPEG only. For 1:1, offer over the friend link rather than a room.
entries.risks: Decoding untrusted images in the game process is a crash and exploit surface; fetch must stay click-to-accept, capped in size, and blocked or muted peers ignored. Screenshots leak names and chat, so the offer dialog should say so. Blob storage grows on disk and needs a cleanup setting.

entries.title: What Is This Craft Worth
entries.pitch: Cost to craft from the full recipe tree against recent sale prices on your data centre, with the age of every price shown.
entries.how: Combine get_recipe_tree (RecipeTree), find_owned_items and get_market_prices (UniversalisClient behind MarketCache) into one tool or prompt: price leaves by median recent sale, mark owned quantities as free, and report the age of each price. The crafting_plan prompt gains a 'with prices' variant.
entries.risks: Universalis data is crowd-sourced and can be hours stale; a thin market gives misleading medians. A deep tree asks for many items and must batch within the 20-item call and be polite with the cache. It stays on reading public prices and never touches the market board UI, per HARD-LINES.md; alerts on single listings are deliberately left out.

entries.title: Next Three Upgrades
entries.pitch: For your current job, the three cheapest item-level gains you can reach, what each costs in tomestones, seals or crafted materials, and what you already hold towards it.
entries.how: A plan_gear_upgrades tool (GameData, with a live half) takes get_equipment's slots, searches equippable items above each slot's level with the same index search_items uses, ranks by item level gain per unit cost from ItemSources (SpecialShop and GilShop rows) and RecipeTree, and compares against get_currencies and find_owned_items. The gear_audit prompt calls it.
entries.risks: Real best-in-slot depends on stat tiers and substat weights the game data does not state; this ranks by item level and cost only, and must say so. SpecialShop parsing is the messiest data in the sheets. Raid drops are not in the sheets at all.

entries.title: Now Playing on Your Lantern
entries.pitch: With XivLantern installed, your friends can see what you are listening to next to your lit lantern, if you say so.
entries.how: XivPiano already offers XivPiano.NowPlaying over IPC. XivLantern would gain an opt-in to read it and add 'listening to' to the presence note it already shares with friends; nothing in XivPiano changes except a new XivPiano.SongChanged message gate (see piano-song-events) so XivLantern does not have to poll. Off by default in both plugins.
entries.risks: It needs work in XivLantern, which only has XivLantern.v1.GetStatus today, and XivLantern's promise is that nothing from the game is sent; a song title is not from the game, but it is still something about you going to others, so it must be plainly opt-in. Song titles can be long and need cutting.

entries.title: The Aethernet Leg
entries.pitch: In the big cities, name the aethernet shard nearest the target as well: 'Teleport to Ul'dah, then aethernet to Sapphire Avenue Exchange'.
entries.how: The Aetheryte sheet includes aethernet shards (not IsAetheryte, grouped by AethernetGroup), with MapMarker positions like the main aetherytes. Extend GameReader.AetherytesIn to return shards, and TargetPicker.NearestAetheryte to pick a (main, shard) pair when the shard saves real distance. Also useful in the same zone: 'aethernet to X' when the walk is long.
entries.risks: Shard attunement state needs its own check, and it may not be exposed as simply as IAetheryteList. Cities span several territories (Ul'dah Steps of Nald and Thal), so the shard graph crosses zones. The note gets longer and must stay readable.

entries.title: Warmer, Colder
entries.pitch: An optional soft chime that repeats faster as you face the right way and slows as you turn away, for players who would rather listen than look.
entries.how: Heading.TurnAway already gives 0 to 1 for how far off course you face. A new pure Chime class in XivWayfinder.Core maps that and the distance to an interval, host-tested like Pulse. The plugin plays a game UI sound through FFXIVClientStructs' UIGlobals.PlaySoundEffect on each tick. Settings: off by default, a sound choice from the chat <se.1>-<se.16> set, and a volume note pointing at the game's own System Sounds slider.
entries.risks: The game's sound effects cannot be pitched, so only the rate can carry meaning. Repeated chimes get tiring fast; it must stop on arrival and in the same situations Visibility.Decide hides the pointer. UIGlobals signatures can move between patches.

entries.title: A Glove on the Compass
entries.pitch: A small glove clings to the edge of the minimap and points the way there too, for players who navigate by the minimap.
entries.how: Read the _NaviMap addon's position, scale and rotation through IGameGui.GetAddonByName and its node tree. Place the glove on the ring with a circular version of ScreenEdge.RayToEdge (a new pure helper in Core, host-tested), and draw it with the existing Glove.Quad and GloveTexture, at a smaller size, on the same foreground draw list Overlay uses.
entries.risks: The minimap can be locked north-up or to the camera, and its rotation must be read correctly for both. HUD layouts, scaling and minimap replacement plugins move or hide it. Addon node indices change between patches.

entries.title: Sightseeing Log Guide
entries.pitch: Point at the next Sightseeing Log vista you have not logged, and say which weather and hours it needs.
entries.how: The Adventure sheet has each vista's Level (place), emote and time window; PlayerState knows which are complete. A new source reads them for the current expansion's log. The existing DrawNote glass note carries the conditions. Pure selection logic goes in Core with host tests, like QuestPick.
entries.risks: Weather conditions come from another sheet and forecasting them is its own project. Needs care to not spoil vistas for players who like finding them unaided, so it only points at the one you ask for.

entries.title: Linkpearl Bridge
entries.pitch: Bridge your FC's Matrix or IRC room into a linkshell-styled terminal that echoes lines only into your local chat log.
entries.how: weechat script emits OSC 777 on activity; surface on_notify to Lua (or an agent NOTIFY frame). Shim forwards IChatGui.Print, which is local-only. Lua filters, colors and rate-limits with a clearly non-game tag.
entries.risks: Low novelty. Chat logger plugins capture external messages. A tag resembling [LS1] invites replying in game chat. Throttle to avoid flooding mid-duty.

entries.title: Stuck? Ask the Scholar
entries.pitch: A spoiler-careful hint button for the game you are playing, answered by your local model through Almanac, with nothing leaving your machine.
entries.how: ArcadeWindow's details strip gets a Hint box that calls Almanac's IPC with the game's title, console and year from ArcadeGame plus the player's own question and a spoiler level. XivArcade sends nothing else: no emulator memory, no screenshots. The reply opens in Almanac's own chat window.
entries.risks: Local models know little about most 1990s games and will invent walkthrough steps; the answer needs a clear 'model guess' label. Depends on Almanac being installed and a model loaded. Adds one more optional cross-plugin IPC to test.

entries.title: Verified Dump Badges
entries.pitch: Check your files against a No-Intro or Redump DAT you supply and mark good dumps, bad dumps and their canonical names.
entries.how: The player drops Logiqx XML DAT files into a dats/ folder; nothing is downloaded. The helper hashes files in the background (SHA-1 and CRC32, cached in the games table by size and mtime), matches them, and puts the verdict and canonical name into state.json. art_candidates tries the canonical name first. Uses the same content-check approach as check_bios_file.
entries.risks: Hashing a PS2 library takes a long time and must be resumable and throttled. CHD and CSO are compressed, so their hashes do not match Redump without chdman or decompression; say 'not checkable' rather than guess. DAT files have their own licensing and must never be bundled.

entries.title: Invite by Name Card
entries.pitch: Send a friend invite to someone's nostr npub or name@domain instead of pasting a ticket through a tell or Discord.
entries.how: nostr_send_invite and nostr_check_inbox are implemented and tested against an in-process relay (tests/nostr.rs), raising NostrInvite without redeeming anything. Add them to lantern-ffi as new LT_EV_* events, NIP-05 resolution as DESIGN.md describes, and an npub field plus pending list in MainWindow.DrawAdd. Accepting still goes through AcceptInvite, so nothing is accepted for the player.
entries.risks: A public npub invites spam; rate limits and ignore must apply to nostr invites too. NIP-05 depends on someone's web server being up. It adds a third party (nostr relays) that the privacy note must name.

entries.title: Moving House
entries.pitch: Export your identity and friend list to one encrypted file and import it on a new PC, so friends do not have to re-add you.
entries.how: The store already holds everything: identity, profile, friends, friend_devices, blocked. Add export and import to lantern-core (a passphrase-encrypted SQLite backup plus a schema version check), expose them in lantern-ffi, and put two buttons in MainWindow.DrawSettings. Saved channel tickets live in the Dalamud Configuration and would be included from the C# side.
entries.risks: Running two copies of the same NodeId at once confuses friends' links and presence; import should refuse while another node with that id is online, which is hard to know. The export file is a full identity and must be treated like a private key.

entries.title: Keys That Open Only Some Doors
entries.pitch: Each per-client token carries its own list of categories, so the benchmark client can read game data but never your chat or your bags.
entries.how: ClientTokenEntry (AutoApprovePolicy.cs) gains an optional category allow-list, edited in MainWindow.Policy.cs and settable through XivMcp.ConnectClient. The request scope already knows which token authenticated; tools/list, resources/list and dispatch filter by it after HostState's global tiers and categories, so a scope can only narrow. Changing a token's scope sends list_changed to that client's sessions only.
entries.risks: Core/Abstractions and McpServer's public surface are frozen, so this must be an additive hook. Clients without a per-client token share the global view, which the UI must make obvious. Resources and templates cut across categories (ffxiv://chat/recent) and need their own mapping. It is a boundary between clients, not a sandbox for a hostile one.

entries.title: Crossfade Between Songs
entries.pitch: Fade the end of one song into the start of the next, so the radio flows like a mix instead of stopping and starting.
entries.how: AudioOut today holds one WaveOutEvent and one MpegSampleProvider. It would build one output over a MixingSampleProvider fed by two MpegSampleProviders, with a PrepareAsync(Track) that downloads the next song while the current one plays (Radio.AdvanceAsync already keeps one song in hand in its queue). A fade of a few seconds starts when Position reaches Duration minus the fade length, and the Ended event moves to the fade start so Radio advances then. Crossfade length and 'off' go in Configuration.
entries.risks: Two songs in memory at once, a few MB each, which is fine. Thumbs and 'why this song?' act on Radio.Current, so the switch-over moment must be clear or a thumb could land on the wrong song. Replay gain differs per song; each keeps its own gain factor. Songs with long silent endings make the fade point a guess.

entries.title: Scrobble to Last.fm
entries.pitch: Send what you listen to in game to your Last.fm profile, as Elpis does, if you sign in to Last.fm.
entries.how: A small Last.fm client in XivPiano.Core (Elpis has one in Libs/LastFmScrobbler): desktop auth once, then track.updateNowPlaying when Radio.Current changes and track.scrobble when a song has played for half its length or four minutes, measured from AudioOut.Position, queued and retried while offline. The session key is kept with Secrets (DPAPI) like the Pandora password. Needs a Last.fm API key registered for XivPiano.
entries.risks: A second network destination, which the privacy note must name, and off by default. Last.fm's own terms apply to the API key. Skipped and banned songs must not scrobble. Scrobble rules about minimum length (30 seconds) must be kept.

entries.title: Real Icons, Not Letter Tiles
entries.pitch: Have ghostty-agent rasterise SVG-only icons once on the host so the grid and taskbar stop falling back to letter tiles.
entries.how: IconResolver already reports IconKind.SvgOnly. Collect those names after a scan and ask the agent for a PNG cache path per name at Configuration.IconSize (a new agent method, rendered with whatever the host has, such as rsvg); cache under XDG_CACHE_HOME keyed by source path and mtime, then map through HostPaths.ToLocal so ITextureProvider opens it. No new dependency in the plugin.
entries.risks: Needs a ghostty-dalamud and agent change, so it only helps players on a matching build. Without the agent, letter tiles remain. Icon themes vary; the cache has to be invalidated when themes change.

entries.title: Lock the Lantern
entries.pitch: Optionally protect the device key (and nostr key) in the node's database with a passphrase, entered when you turn Lantern on.
entries.how: DESIGN.md's threat model says the key sits unencrypted like an SSH key with no passphrase. Wrap the identity row and the nostr_secret profile row with a key derived by Argon2id, add an unlock parameter to lt_config (an lt_node_open error code for 'locked'), and a passphrase prompt in MainWindow.DrawWelcome before LanternService.Start. Existing databases migrate on first set.
entries.risks: A forgotten passphrase loses the identity for good; there is deliberately no recovery. Auto-start at plugin load (config.Enabled) can no longer be silent. The ABI version must bump.

entries.title: Your Agents Are a Light Party
entries.pitch: Parallel Claude Code agents fight at your side as a light party: tank plans, healer reviews, two DPS implement in their own worktrees, with context as MP and every tool call as a cast.
entries.how: `ghostty-party` reads a composition from lua/party.lua (role, job icon, prompt file, worktree), runs `git worktree add` per member, and OPENs `claude` with a CWD env entry and a GHOSTTY_SESSION variable. Claude Code hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification, PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStop) call a tiny `ghostty-emit` that writes to a new unix socket on ghostty-agent, which buffers EVENT frames for detached sessions and broadcasts them; MP comes from the last usage entry in the hook's transcript_path. Formation is a new anchor preset on the pet springs in lua/world.lua, and frames are ImGui with job icons from ITextureProvider.GetFromGameIcon. Agents running outside Ghostty join through an in-game MCP server plugin: the shim subscribes to that plugin's agent-board IPC and change event and turns its status posts into frames. The LB button only types `git merge` into the tank's session with `/term type`, never Enter.
entries.risks: Four live agents cost real money and quota, so the party list shows spend. Hook payloads and tool names change between Claude Code releases. Sharing with the FC puts code, prompts and secrets on other clients, and every attached client can write today, so it needs a read-only relay, a share toggle and redaction. Worktrees pile up and need an explicit disband. Inside duties the formation collapses to frames only. No in-game MCP server has been observed working yet.

entries.title: Keep Typing and Nobody Derezzes
entries.pitch: An asymmetric bomb-defusal party game: one player's terminal holds the ticking bomb and everyone else's holds a different page of the manual.
entries.how: A game-master script on the host's agent generates a puzzle seed, then opens one bomb session and one manual session per reader. Each invite carries a token scoped to one role's session (read-write for the defuser, read-only for readers) and the crate's anchor as a save_state snippet. The bomb TUI emits `ESC _ ffxiv;bomb;strike=1;t=150 ESC \`, which each client catches through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. Lua turns a strike into a red-tinted `sonar` bell style at the crate anchor, a world.nelua glitch on every panel and a short camera jitter through the existing GetCameraState/SetCameraState path. Detonation plays `burst` and derezzes every panel for a beat. Players talk only over voice or chat they type themselves.
entries.risks: Scoped and read-only tokens don't exist yet; today's single token grants a shell. Voice chat is effectively required. Puzzle design is real game-design work. The camera jitter needs a motion-sickness toggle and never fires InCombat or BoundByDuty. Guest sessions need the same sandboxing as any shared shell.

entries.title: Keystroke Colosseum
entries.pitch: Vimgolf duels fought on two towering arena panels, where every keystroke drains your own HP bar and the stands get instant replays.
entries.how: A duel host on the agent opens both contestant sessions from a challenge file inside a container, counts DATA frames per session as keystrokes and runs a checker when the editor exits. Spectators ATTACH to both sessions, and the agent already fans output to every attached client (agent.nelua broadcast). Counts, clock and result arrive as `ffxiv;duel` APCs through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. Lua places both panels with `at` anchors from a shared arena origin and draws HP bars with new ui progress widgets. For instant replay each spectator's client calls ghostty_snapshot_encode_buf once a second per duel terminal into a 15 s ring, and replay decodes each frame with ghostty_snapshot_decoder_decode into a scratch terminal on a replay panel. The derez reuses world.nelua's rez effect and the `burst` bell preset.
entries.risks: Every attached client can write and there's one token, so contestants need session-scoped tokens and spectators a read-only relay before this is safe. Snapshotting two terminals every second costs CPU and memory, so duel sessions use tiny scrollback. DATA frames don't map one-to-one to keystrokes (escape sequences, key repeat), and paste must be disabled or scored by bytes. Contestants run code on the duel box, so the sandbox is mandatory. Players without the plugin see two people typing at thin air.

entries.title: Process Skyline
entries.pitch: Your machine's process table rises as a neon city on your island: memory sets a tower's height, CPU lights its windows, and every fork raises a new building.
entries.how: A helper on the agent host samples /proc every second and writes the changes as `ESC _ ffxiv;procs;<pid ppid rss cpu state comm> ESC \` into a hidden session kept live with run_occluded, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE with OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES raised. Lua lays out a treemap by parent PID at a `here` anchor, so systemd slices become districts, and tower heights move on the same springs world.lua uses for pets. Towers are extruded quads through world_transform_vertices with windows as lit dotted rects, tinted by world.lighting(). Hovering uses ray-box tests built on the world_hit maths, and double-click opens a panel whose profile runs `htop -p <pid>`.
entries.risks: Hundreds of processes means hundreds of extruded ImGui boxes, so threads merge, small processes bucket into suburbs and draw calls are capped. Extrusions have no depth test unless routed through the depth pass, so the city shows through hills. Command lines leak tokens in argv, so arguments are hidden by default. On a busy desktop it's just a Chrome city without a filter.

entries.title: The Lighting Desk
entries.pitch: A tracker or cue sheet in a terminal drives a rig of real in-game lights channel by channel, and opted-in patrons at the venue see the same show on their own clients.
entries.how: On the host, `ffxiv-lightd` reads the tracker's MIDI out (ALSA sequencer or JACK) or a cue script and prints `ESC _ ffxiv;cue;ch=1;n=36;v=127;t=183.250 ESC \` into a desk session; the APCs never touch the grid and arrive through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE only on sessions flagged as desks. A new lua/lightrig.lua maps channels to fixtures (offset from a pinned `here` anchor, colour, range, shadows, attack and decay), and app/lights.nelua grows from one light per panel into a capped pool on the same LightCreate/LightUpdate calls (HostApi.cs:400-451). Patrons ATTACH to the desk session: the agent already broadcasts output to every attached client and replays 256 KiB on join. Cues carry desk time, and a new agent timestamp frame lets clients schedule against a playout buffer of about 150 ms. Fixture offsets hang off the house's ward, plot and room, which an in-game MCP server plugin can already read through HousingManager.
entries.risks: Every attached client can write today and there's a single token, so patrons need a read-only broadcast relay first. Nobody knows how many Scene.Lights the renderer tolerates, so cap the pool at 8-16. Strobes need a hard rate limit and a per-patron intensity slider. Sync is only as good as each patron's latency, and the music reaches them over Discord or Twitch with its own drift. Players without the plugin see a normal club. Aetherial Visualizer pulses panels from local audio; this is an authored, shared show.

entries.title: Link Cable over Lantern
entries.pitch: Invite a friend from XivLantern to a RetroArch netplay session of a game you both own, with the connection details passed privately between you.
entries.how: The helper's launch_argv gains RetroArch's host and connect netplay modes. XivArcade offers a new IPC call beside XivArcade.v1.Search and Launch that builds an invite: game_id, core name and version, content CRC and a tailnet or LAN address, never the file. XivLantern carries it peer to peer, and the receiving XivArcade checks that the same game_id with the same CRC is in its own library before offering Join.
entries.risks: The hard line holds: no game file, disc or BIOS ever travels, and a CRC mismatch refuses. NAT traversal is hard without Tailscale or a relay. Netplay needs identical core versions and breaks with standalone emulators. Needs a Lantern IPC hook that does not exist yet, and RetroArch netplay latency inside a headless compositor is unknown.

entries.title: Ring a Friend
entries.pitch: One-to-one voice calls: ring from the friend list, and the audio runs in a small companion process beside the game.
entries.how: Follows DESIGN.md's call plan. Signalling already exists as a spike behind the calls feature (node/calls.rs: CallRing, CallAnswer, CallHangup with an iroh://<node>/call/<id> media URL); it needs C ABI events and a MainWindow call bar. Media runs in a lantern-media sidecar using moq-native with iroh and moq-audio against PipeWire (or WASAPI on Windows), paired to the plugin's node by a one-time ticket like a friend invite and driven over a loopback friend link.
entries.risks: None of the media path has been built; DESIGN.md lists four observable steps before anything is in the game. Shipping and starting a second executable from a Dalamud plugin is unusual and must be explicit to the player. Echo cancellation, NAT traversal for UDP media and latency are all unmeasured.

entries.title: The Server Room
entries.pitch: One glowing panel per homelab node, pinned in your house or to housing furniture, with backlight and derez driven by live health checks.
entries.how: Health comes from a hidden capture session or agent probes (ping/tcp/http, node_exporter, incus list) via a new STATUS/EVENT frame, never from the panels, which sleep. Lua maps host to ok/warn/down and sets per-panel tint/backlight; move rez from global host.world_rez to per session in worldview.nelua. Placement uses house-id-aware anchors (see furniture-anchors). Drill-in reuses click focus, fly-in and per-host ssh profiles. Shared view uses read-only guest tokens (see over-the-shoulder-pets).
entries.risks: No depth test, so panels show through walls. A dozen live btop panels cost real FPS. Housing structs move between patches. Probe flaps cause alert fatigue; this is not a pager. Showing dashboards to an FC leaks hostnames and IPs.

entries.title: Item Links in stdout
entries.pitch: OSC 8 links with an ffxiv:// scheme turn CLI output into item tooltips, map flags and chat-ready item links.
entries.how: Mouse to cell to GhosttyGridRef, then ghostty_grid_ref_hyperlink_uri, sharing mouse-selection plumbing. Lua parses item/map/quest URIs into typed actions. Shim forwards Lumina Item lookup and icon, OpenMapWithMapLink, and a chat-input item link insert. ImGui tooltip first; native tooltip later.
entries.risks: Output is untrusted: typed actions only, click required, never free text into chat. Chat-input insertion depends on unstable ClientStructs internals.

entries.title: Kitty Graphics Tapestries
entries.pitch: Kitty graphics protocol images render on 3D panels, so live dashboards and pictures hang in the world like paintings.
entries.how: libghostty-vt already implements kitty graphics placements. Decode PNG with vendored stb_image or Zig. Shim forwards CreateTexture/ReleaseTexture via ITextureProvider.CreateFromRaw, cached by image id. Draw placements as tessellated quads so world_transform_vertices curves and tints them; plain AddImage in 2D. No sixel.
entries.risks: Images vanish past the replay ring on sleep or restart unless re-sent or cached agent-side. Cap texture memory in-process; create on the render thread and free on unload or crash.

entries.title: Pass the Model M
entries.pitch: Pair-program with a party member in one tmux session, and the floating Model M flies to whoever holds the keys.
entries.how: Agent already fans output to multiple attached clients. Add scoped guest tokens (session ids, ro/rw), a per-session driver, and DRIVER/PASS frames over a tailnet. Lua 'between' anchor at the midpoint of player and friend; Model M springs between them on driver events. Each client poses only its own character.
entries.risks: Guest tokens are a new security boundary on a TLS-less agent, so tailnet only; rw means arbitrary code as the host user. Seeing your friend's pose locally is unproven. Depends on the in-progress Model M.

entries.title: Allagan Phosphor
entries.pitch: Every terminal re-renders in the technology of wherever you stand: Allagan green phosphor, Garlean magitek amber, Sharlayan hologram blue, Crystarium cut glass.
entries.how: Draw each world panel's cells into an offscreen texture with ITextureProvider.CreateDrawListTexture, only when the render state reports GHOSTTY_RENDER_STATE_DIRTY_PARTIAL or FULL, so idle panels cost nothing. Draw that texture on the curved quad through the core/depthpass.nelua callbacks with a material shader built by tools/build-shaders.lua: barrel curvature, shadow mask, scanlines, bloom, and persistence blended with last frame's texture. The glass material also copies the panel's screen rect from the back buffer and offsets its samples by the cylinder normal panel_depth.hlsl already computes. A new lua/materials.lua maps TerritoryType through Lumina to material tables, world.place gains a `material` field, and zone changes crossfade. While DATA_MODE shows synchronized output (2026) the texture keeps its last frame so trails never smear a half-drawn screen. Cracks key off the agent-side CMD_END exit code.
entries.risks: Render-to-texture adds a pass and texture memory per dirty panel, and it's unconfirmed that CreateDrawListTexture accepts a draw list built by the native core, so a direct-draw fallback stays. The back-buffer copy is taken after the HUD is drawn, so HUD pieces behind glass bend too. Curvature and bloom cost legibility, so a hold-to-read key snaps back to crisp. Persistence trails can bother motion-sensitive players. Nothing on the depth path has been observed in game.

entries.title: Two-Person Rule by Emote
entries.pitch: Gate a dangerous command behind signed approvals from party members, with /thumbsup as the ritual.
entries.how: Authority lives in the agent: held command, quorum policy, approver public keys, ed25519 verify via vendored monocypher over (hash, nonce, expiry), then forkpty. Frames PENDING/APPROVE/APPROVED. Approver's plugin watches only its own timeline for thumbsup (or /term approve), signs and sends over a guest connection.
entries.risks: Keys inside the game process are readable by other plugins; pitch as oops-prevention, not security, with a hardware-key option. Enforce minimum view time on the diff. Real crypto in a hobby agent needs care.

entries.title: The Cabinet in the Corner
entries.pitch: Give a game a fixed spot in your house or apartment, so it always opens on the same wall or furniture instead of wherever the panel lands.
entries.how: Today ArcadeService.Play hands one shell line to HostLauncher.RunInCompositor, which sends window.open with only a run field, then finds the panel through window.list. Add an optional placement to GhosttyWire.OpenRun (anchor position, heading, size, territory and house id), stored per game in Configuration and captured with '/arcade cabinet here' from the player's own position. ghostty-dalamud needs a matching window.open parameter or a window.place call; its own furniture-anchor idea covers the house-id side.
entries.risks: It depends on a ghostty-dalamud IPC change that does not exist yet. Housing layout and territory ids shift with patches, and panels have no depth test, so a cabinet can show through walls. The panel path has not been observed in game at all.

entries.title: Turn a Conversation into a Benchmark Task
entries.pitch: When a model gets a real question badly wrong, turn that exchange into a proposed benchmark task, with the tool results frozen as fixtures, for the next suite version.
entries.how: A thread already holds the user prompt, each tool call and its JSON result, which are the shape of a SuiteTask (Prompt, Tools, Expect) and of the suite's fixtures that FixtureToolSource replays. Build the draft task from AlmanacStore.Messages, let the player write the Expect rules in the vocabulary JsonRules and Scorer already use, and send it through the existing DeviceLink sign-in to a proposals endpoint, not straight into ffxiv-core.
entries.risks: Fixtures captured live contain the character name, location history, retainers and possibly other players' names from chat tools; the form has to redact them and show the exact payload, as Share does. Every accepted task changes the suite's Sha256 and breaks comparability with past runs, so tasks must batch into versioned releases. Writing good Expect rules is hard for most players.

entries.title: Aetherial Visualizer
entries.pitch: Audio from a terminal's player makes panel backlights and pet terminals pulse to the beat.
entries.how: Agent matches PipeWire nodes to the PTY process tree, captures with pw-record, runs a windowed FFT, and sends 8-16 bands as a BANDS frame at 30-60Hz. Lua modulates backlight and adds pet spring impulses; bars are extra projected quads.
entries.risks: Audio over ssh plays remotely and can't be captured. Crowds see nothing unless synced. Needs intensity cap and photosensitivity toggle. Flatpak and pulse-compat matching is fragile.

entries.title: Blueprints with Ghost Furniture
entries.pitch: Share a terminal installation as a paste-able blueprint, or import a MakePlace layout, that projects wireframe outlines where the furniture goes.
entries.how: Builds on furniture-anchors. Lua serializes anchors plus item id and relative transform to base64 and imports MakePlace JSON. Nelua draws projected wireframe boxes sized from a per-item table. Match detection by item id within tolerance; template form in views.nelua; warm-up reuses rez.
entries.risks: Must never write furniture positions: show a match indicator and let the player place. Shared commands are an RCE vector, so never auto-run and hash-pin blueprints. Only transfers between identical house sizes.

entries.title: Paged Mid-Pull
entries.pitch: When your on-call healer gets paged, opted-in party members see a status line over them, so everyone knows why they went AFK.
entries.how: Webhook receiver pushes a templated STATUS frame to the on-call's agent. Party members hold status-only guest tokens. Map name@world to entity via IPartyList/object table and project an ImGui label above the head. Incident terminal reuses over-the-shoulder-pets.
entries.risks: Alert text leaks infra details; templated and redacted only. Ship as a mode of over-the-shoulder-pets and the bell, not a separate system. Hide labels in combat.

entries.title: Catch Up on Join
entries.pitch: Someone who joins or comes back to a channel gets the recent backlog from any member who has it, instead of an empty room.
entries.how: DESIGN.md already names the shape: a blob snapshot offered by any member. Keep the signed gossip frames per channel in a new store table, and on a peer's Hello offer a snapshot with lt_blob_add_bytes and lt_blob_offer, which exist in the C ABI and the C# binding (BlobAddBytes, BlobOffer, BlobFetch) but are unused by the plugin today. The joiner fetches, re-verifies every frame with proto.rs, de-duplicates by signature and merges into ChatBook through Conversation.LoadHistory.
entries.risks: Gossip gives no ordering, so merged history needs a sort by sender timestamp that a member could lie about. Every member keeps a copy, which makes 'delete' meaningless and should be said plainly. Snapshot size and how far back need limits, and a malicious member can offer junk, so verification must drop anything unsigned.

entries.title: The FC Hearth
entries.pitch: One container an FC can run on a spare box: an iroh relay, a moq relay for group calls, and an always-on node that keeps channel history.
entries.how: Relay choice already supports LT_RELAY_CUSTOM with a URL (Configuration.CustomRelayUrl, Privacy.Relay). Package iroh-relay, moq-relay and a headless lantern-cli node (the CLI already runs author mode, so a 'keeper' mode that joins listed channels and serves history snapshots fits) as one OCI image with a compose file and a README of who sees what. Group calls use the relay for fan-out per the DESIGN.md plan.
entries.risks: Whoever runs it sees IP addresses and timing for everyone who uses it, and holds every channel's plaintext if channels are not sealed; the privacy note must name them. Home hosting means port forwarding or tunnels. Keeping three services patched is a real commitment for a volunteer.

entries.title: Leave It at the Post
entries.pitch: When a friend has been offline for a while, your message also goes to their nostr inbox, so it reaches them even if you are both never online at once.
entries.how: DESIGN.md specifies it: NIP-17 kind 14 rumor, sealed and gift-wrapped to the friend's DM relays, carrying the Lantern message id so the iroh copy is dropped as a duplicate. The nostr feature already sends invites this way (nostr_send_invite, nostr_check_inbox in node/nostr.rs); extend it to texts in the outbox, then expose nostr in the C ABI, which it is not today, and add a relay list to Configuration.
entries.risks: Relays learn who receives messages, when and how big. It needs both people to have opted into nostr keys, and the nostr secret sits unencrypted in SQLite. Relays drop old events on their own schedule, so delivery is best effort and the UI must not promise more.

entries.title: Other Plugins Can Offer Tools
entries.pitch: An IPC gate through which any Dalamud plugin registers its own read tools with XivMcp, under the same catalogue, rate limit and approval gate.
entries.how: Core already describes tools by data through ExternalTool (McpServer.Extensions.cs), which the standalone host uses. A new IpcContract gate lets a plugin register ExternalTool descriptions whose handler calls back into that plugin's own IPC. They sit under a per-plugin category the player enables in Settings, and anything not Read goes through ConfirmationService like every other gated tool.
entries.risks: XivMcp cannot see what another plugin's handler does, so HARD-LINES.md cannot be enforced on it; the first version should allow Read tier only, and say so. ToolContractTests cannot check runtime tools. A plugin that unloads leaves dead tools until list_changed. IpcContract is a frozen, additive-only contract.

entries.title: Commit Constellations
entries.pitch: On clear in-game nights, your git history hangs in the sky as constellations.
entries.how: Hidden agent session runs `git log --graph`. sky.lua lays nodes on a camera dome gated by GetEnvironment time, weather and rain. Stars drawn and hit-tested in worldview.nelua with the existing fly-in. Stretch: sky-only occlusion by sampling the depth buffer, as Pictomancy does.
entries.risks: Without depth occlusion stars draw over rooftops and the illusion breaks. Large graphs don't read as constellations. Decorative and rarely looked at.

entries.title: Job Codex Terminals
entries.pitch: The terminal's physical form follows your job: codex pages for Scholar, a star globe for Astrologian, a wrist hologram for Machinist.
entries.how: Add ClassJob to GuObject. Lua style table per job selects frame, layout and pose. Nelua render variants: page-flip transition, spherical strip, rune/hologram overlays on existing scanline code. Page flip triggered by tmux window change. Bone anchoring is stretch; pet offset as fallback.
entries.risks: Per-job art and tuning is a large surface for a niche payoff; ship two or three. Bone positions vary by race and scale.

entries.title: OBS Scene Conductor
entries.pitch: Duty and panel events switch OBS scenes, and stream triggers fire whitelisted cosmetic effects in game.
entries.how: Shim forwards IDutyState and TerritoryChanged; core sends EVENT frames to the agent. A small sidecar speaks obs-websocket v5 and relays inbound events as EFFECT frames. lua/effects.lua maps them to whitelisted calls gated on InCombat and BoundByDuty.
entries.risks: Viewer camera control is risky if a gate fails. The agent holds another credential and any network exposure widens a shell-granting service. Frame-locked browser overlays are dropped.

entries.title: Moogle Delivery for App Notifications
entries.pitch: Show notifications from apps running in the compositor as Dalamud toasts, with the app's icon and a click that focuses its panel.
entries.how: The agent owns org.freedesktop.Notifications on the session bus it gives its compositor's apps and forwards summary, body and app id as a new event in window.list or a separate method. SessionService already raises Dalamud notifications through INotificationManager for panel open and end; extend Notify with the app's icon from CatalogService and a click that runs PaletteCommand.Focus.
entries.risks: Depends entirely on agent changes and on apps using the session bus the agent controls. Notification bodies are private and would show on stream; needs a 'title only' option. Rate limiting is needed for chatty apps.

entries.title: One Friend, Every Device
entries.pitch: A friend who plays on a PC and a Steam Deck is one entry, and messages reach whichever device they are on.
entries.how: The core already models friends with many devices (friends and friend_devices tables) and verifies nostr device lists (nostr_publish_devices, nostr_fetch_devices, the lantern-device-claim/1 signature). What is missing is text fan-out to all devices with de-duplication by message id across them, the nostr calls in lantern-ffi and include/lantern.h, and a 'this device / add a device' page in MainWindow.DrawSettings.
entries.risks: Delivered and read state across devices gets confusing fast (delivered to the PC, read on the Deck). Adding a device means importing the nsec on each, which moves a secret between machines. DESIGN.md lists this as the known gap because it is real work.

entries.title: Sealed Channels
entries.pitch: Channel messages encrypted with a key carried in the ticket, so relays and nodes passing gossip along cannot read them.
entries.how: Add a symmetric key to the ltroom ticket in ticket.rs and encrypt the payload inside the signed frame in proto.rs (XChaCha20-Poly1305, signature over the ciphertext). Scope::Custom topics stay random. 'Reseal' makes a new channel with a new key and sends ChannelInvite over each chosen friend link, which friends.rs already does. The plugin shows a lock in DrawList and the ticket wording changes in DrawAdd.
entries.risks: Anyone holding the ticket still reads everything; this protects against the swarm, not against members. Removing a member is only a reseal, and old keys still read old history. A ticket format change needs a version byte and a clear message on old clients.

entries.title: Walk, Don't Teleport
entries.pitch: When the target is one or two zones away on foot, point at the zone exit instead of naming an aetheryte.
entries.how: Map-to-map links come from MapMarker rows of the map-link type, read the same way GameReader.AetherytesIn already reads aetheryte markers and converted with MapCoords.PixelToWorld. Build a zone graph once and find the shortest walk with a breadth-first search in Core (pure, host-tested).
