TargetPicker.Plan grows a WalkToExit guide kind; GetState's 'guide' field gains a value, documented in IPC.md.
entries.risks: Links through ferries, airships and NPC dialogue are not walkable and are hard to tell apart from real exits. One-way drops and locked zones (before a quest opens them) will mislead. Deciding when walking beats teleporting is a judgement call, so the first version should only offer it for adjacent zones.

entries.title: Only the Tools the Question Needs
entries.pitch: Before each turn, narrow the offered tools to the few that fit the question, so small models stop reaching for get_equipment when you asked about the weather.
entries.how: ToolProfiles' own comment says small models do better with fewer tools; today the choice is a static small/standard/all set. Add a per-turn filter to ToolHub: score each ToolDef by keyword overlap and, where the server offers one, embeddings from an /v1/embeddings model, keep the top N plus a fixed core (get_location, get_player). Measure it with BenchRunner against the unfiltered sets before it becomes a default.
entries.risks: Leaving out the tool a question needed is worse than offering too many: the model guesses. Embeddings need a second model loaded next to the chat model and the game. Changing the tool list between turns of one thread can confuse models that cache tool names, and it makes benchmark results incomparable unless recorded in the result.

entries.title: Media Keys and Hotkeys
entries.pitch: Play, pause and skip with your keyboard's media keys, or a key of your choosing, while the game has focus.
entries.how: Dalamud's IKeyState reads keys while the game window has focus; Plugin.OnUpdate would watch the media keys (VK_MEDIA_PLAY_PAUSE, VK_MEDIA_NEXT_TRACK) and any keys set in Configuration, and call Plugin.Control('toggle') or Control('next') on a fresh press. Elpis does the same outside a game with global hotkeys (Elpis/Hotkeys.cs); here only in-focus keys are planned.
entries.risks: Whether Wine passes media keys to the game at all has to be found out, and the desktop's own media player may take them first. A bound key must not also trigger a game action, and IKeyState cannot stop the game seeing it, so plain keys are risky and chords are safer. Macros with /piano already cover most of this.

entries.title: Magic Lantern
entries.pitch: Aim a panel like a projector and its terminal, text and kitty images alike, is thrown onto whatever it hits: walls, furniture, aetherytes and the people walking through the beam.
entries.how: The projector's terminal is drawn into a texture (ITextureProvider.CreateDrawListTexture from the shim, or a D3D11 render target on the device GuSceneDepth.ui_device already exposes), with kitty images uploaded through the decode path Kitty Graphics Tapestries needs: GHOSTTY_SYS_OPT_DECODE_PNG, re-uploaded when GHOSTTY_KITTY_IMAGE_DATA_GENERATION changes. A full-screen quad then runs through the same draw-list callbacks as core/depthpass.nelua with a sibling of panel_depth.hlsl: it rebuilds each pixel's world position from the reversed-Z SceneDepth and the inverse view-projection rows that cbuffer already carries, moves it into the projector's frustum from its world.place() pose, and samples the texture with cone falloff and a facing term from depth derivatives. app/lights.nelua tints the panel's Scene.Light toward the frame's average colour, so the room's real lighting brightens too. Alt-drag and Shift-snap aim it.
entries.risks: It adds colour over a finished frame; it isn't real lighting, and it lands behind water, glass and hair that don't write depth. Render-to-texture from the native core is unproven, and the depth path has only been checked in a Wine/DXVK probe. Kitty's shm medium doesn't cross the TCP agent, so video arrives as base64 frames: cap resolution and FPS. Flashing video needs a photosensitivity switch. Only you and your stream see it.

entries.title: Paint the Sky
entries.pitch: Pipe a pixel shader from your shell and it replaces the sky over Eorzea on your screen only, fed by Eorzea time, the weather and where your camera points.
entries.how: A shell helper compiles the HLSL on the Linux host with the same pinned vkd3d-compiler tools/build-shaders.lua uses, so nothing compiles inside Wine, and sends the DXBC as `ESC _ ffxiv;sky;<base64> ESC \`, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE with OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES and OPT_APC_MAX_BYTES raised for the payload. The core checks the DXBC header, creates the pixel shader on GuSceneDepth.ui_device, and adds one full-screen quad at the start of the background draw list through the core/depthpass.nelua callback path, with SceneDepth still bound at t1. The shader keeps only pixels whose reversed-Z depth is 0 (the infinite far plane) and discards the rest. A fixed cbuffer supplies day seconds, rain and weather id from ghostty.env(), the camera-relative inverse view-projection rows panel_depth.hlsl already builds rays from, the depth sizes and the session's bell count.
entries.risks: Nobody has checked that the sky really reads depth 0; `/term depth show` comes first. A painted sky hides the sun, moon and clouds, and effects that don't write depth leave odd edges. Shader bytecode from a shell runs on your GPU inside the game process, where a heavy shader can stall frames or remove the device, so accept it only from the focused session, time-box it, and ask before loading one from a remote host. Only you and your stream see it.

entries.title: The Tablet Prop Shows Your Shell
entries.pitch: The tablet or book your character holds shows your live terminal on the game model itself.
entries.how: Render the terminal to an offscreen texture (ITextureProvider draw-list wrap or D3D11 from Nelua), walk Character to weapon CharacterBase to Material texture, and swap its shader resource view each frame; a Penumbra mod gives a clean UV region. Cheap fallback: forward the hand bone world position and pin a small curved panel there.
entries.risks: Pointer-swapping game textures risks use-after-free crashes on zoning, redraws and Penumbra reloads. Shared texture shows your shell on every visible instance of that prop. Barely readable outside close-ups.

entries.title: Push to Talk, Read Aloud
entries.pitch: Hold a key, ask your question out loud, and hear the answer spoken, with speech recognition and voice both running on your own machine.
entries.how: Capture microphone audio in the plugin (for example NAudio's WASAPI capture), send it to a local whisper.cpp server's /inference endpoint that ServerDetector could find like the model servers, and pass the text to ChatWindow.Send. For speech, stream the TextDeltaEvent text sentence by sentence to a local TTS server such as Piper and play it on a separate audio device. Settings hold the two endpoints and the key.
entries.risks: Microphone capture inside the game process under Wine is unreliable, and audio APIs differ per system. Speech recognition and TTS take GPU or CPU next to the chat model and the game, which is exactly the budget the wizard is trying to protect. Picking up voice chat from a party must never happen by accident, so push to talk only, with a clear indicator.

entries.title: Homelab Minion Menagerie
entries.pitch: Each server gets a client-side creature that follows you and acts out its health.
entries.how: Per-host health records over a new agent frame. Existing place_pet springs drive following. Ready fallback: ImGui billboard sprites on the same springs. Real version: client-side actors via ClientObjectManager or Brio IPC, with a BGCollision raycast for ground height and custom screen-space hit tests.
entries.risks: Client-spawned actors outside GPose are a known crash source and a grey area; they must despawn before zoning. Brio spawn outside GPose is uncertain. Many actors cost performance.

entries.title: Send This Window to Eorzea
entries.pitch: A GNOME Shell entry that hands a window already running on your desktop to the game as a panel.
entries.how: Moving an already-mapped window into the agent's compositor is not possible as such; GUIDE.md's planned route is the agent capturing it through the desktop portal's screencast, as it does on Windows. A small Shell extension calls the agent (not Wine) with the window's identity; the agent starts a capture and the game gets a window.open with a match. XivDesktop's part is palette and taskbar support for captured panels.
entries.risks: A captured window is a picture plus forwarded input, not a native panel; input forwarding through the portal is limited. The portal prompts the user every time on many setups. GNOME extension APIs change every release. Nothing of this exists yet.

entries.title: Lantern in Your Pocket
entries.pitch: A small phone app that is one more of your devices, so you can see who is lit and answer a message away from the PC.
entries.how: lantern-core is plain Rust with no game dependency, and lantern-cli already runs it headless. A mobile shell (iroh runs on Android and iOS) would reuse lantern-core, pair as another device through the nostr device list (lantern-every-device), and use the nostr mailbox for wake-ups instead of a push server. Start with the CLI on a Linux phone or Termux as the proof.
entries.risks: Mobile OSes kill background sockets, so presence and delivery need the mailbox or a push service, which reintroduces a server. App store distribution is its own project. Keys on a phone widen where the identity can be stolen from.

entries.title: Voice Without the Sidecar
entries.pitch: Try running Opus capture and playback inside lantern.dll itself, under the game's Wine, so voice needs nothing else installed.
entries.how: Step 5 of DESIGN.md's call plan: build moq-audio (unsafe-libopus, cpal, sonora AEC) for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu in the same container that builds lantern.dll, repeat the WINE.md evidence method with a test prefix, and only then consider the game's prefix. Frames stay off the render thread; the plugin only sees lt_poll events for mute and level.
entries.risks: cpal's WASAPI path under Wine goes through Wine's audio stack, whose latency and device handling vary by distro. A crash in audio code is a game crash, which is the reason the sidecar exists. It may simply not be good enough, and the honest result could be 'no'.

entries.title: Real Rows in the Duty List
entries.pitch: Replace the overlay with native nodes inside the Duty List itself, so custom objectives and agent posts move, collapse and hide exactly as quests do.
entries.how: Option (a) in OBJECTIVES.md: node injection into _ToDoList through IAddonLifecycle (PostSetup, PostRequestedUpdate, PostRefresh, PreFinalize), either through KamiToolKit or Dalamud's native overlay service once goatcorp/Dalamud#2874 is merged. It is a drop-in for ObjectiveOverlay and DutyListAnchor; ObjectiveStore, the evaluator and the tools do not change.
entries.risks: AddonToDoList has no slot for plugin rows and rebuilds its ListPanel itself; a node still linked at finalize (zone change, HUD layout change, unload) crashes the game rather than failing softly. KamiToolKit is a large dependency to keep current with patches. None of it can be tested outside the running game.

entries.title: Listen Together
entries.pitch: A party or linkshell tunes in to the same station's seeds together, each person on their own Pandora account, with play and pause kept in step.
entries.how: The code carries the station's seeds (from station.getStation with includeExtendedAttributes, as pianobar asks for them) as music tokens. Each listener's XivPiano makes a station with station.createStation from the first and adds the rest with station.addMusic, then plays it. Play and pause travel as small messages over XivLantern's channels when it is installed, or not at all. Nothing but the code and play/pause state is shared.
entries.risks: Every listener hears different songs, because Pandora makes a playlist per listener and XivPiano will never pass audio from one player to another (that would be rebroadcasting, which Pandora's terms forbid). So 'together' means the same kind of music, not the same song, and the page must say that honestly. Everyone needs a US Pandora account. It adds a station to each listener's list, which they may not want to keep.

entries.title: A Bead That Knows About Walls
entries.pitch: Draw the bead in the world itself rather than on top of the screen, so a pillar or a companion can stand in front of it the way real things do.
entries.how: Overlay draws everything on ImGui's foreground list, which has no depth. Two routes to try: spawn a client-side VFX at the bead's world position (the approach Splatoon-style plugins take), or read the game's depth buffer and test the bead's projected point against it before drawing. Either way the bead's position stays computed by Heading.Ahead and Pulse, and the ImGui bead remains the fallback.
entries.risks: Both routes need hooks or signatures that break on patches, and a VFX left behind on unload or a crash stays in the scene. Reading the depth buffer is renderer-specific and may not work the same under Wine. May cost more frame time than the whole plugin does today.

entries.title: X Marks the Spot
entries.pitch: Once you have deciphered a timeworn map, point at the dig site it shows.
entries.how: The TreasureSpot and TreasureHuntRank sheets give the candidate Level rows; which one is yours is only known after deciphering. Research whether the client exposes it in an agent (as the treasure-map UI must know it) before considering a hook. The result becomes an Explicit Target, so the aetheryte hint and vnavmesh work unchanged.
entries.risks: If the spot is only in a network packet, reading it means a hook, which is fragile and a larger step than anything the plugin does now. Established plugins already fill this niche. Must never extend to anything the player has not deciphered themselves.

entries.title: Sandboxed WebAssembly Tools
entries.pitch: Let players add small tools, such as a gil calculator or a rotation lookup, as WebAssembly modules that can reach nothing they are not granted.
entries.how: The WasmToolSource sketched in ToolSources.cs's doc comment: one module per tool, exporting its ToolDef JSON and call(args-json) -> result-json, run under WASI with no preopens or sockets by default. It only has to implement IToolSource; Engine.NewLoop adds it to the ToolHub list after XivMcp, so XivMcp keeps name priority. Per-module grants shown in SettingsWindow; the runtime is disposed in Engine.Dispose and counted by LiveObjects so the reload leak tests cover it.
entries.risks: A Wasm runtime such as Wasmtime brings a native library that has to load inside Dalamud on Windows and under Wine, the same class of problem as the SQLite native library, and must unload cleanly on plugin reload. Fuel or time limits are needed so a looping module cannot stall a turn. Sharing modules invites people to run code from strangers; grants must default to nothing.

entries.title: One Clipboard for Both Worlds
entries.pitch: Copy in a host app panel and paste into game chat, or the other way round, through the agent.
entries.how: The game side is Wine's Windows clipboard, reachable from the plugin through ImGui's clipboard functions. The compositor side needs ghostty-agent to act as a Wayland data-device client in its own compositor. XivDesktop would watch for a change on either side and relay text only, with a size cap, through a new agent method; PaletteCommand.Copy already writes the game side.
entries.risks: Needs agent work in ghostty-dalamud. Password managers put secrets on the clipboard, so relaying must be opt-in, text only and skip sensitive MIME hints. Two-way sync loops need care. Wine's clipboard is already bridged to the host X11 or Wayland session on some setups, which could produce three clipboards fighting.

entries.title: Terminal Layouts That Remember the House
entries.pitch: Saved Ghostty layouts tied to a housing plot and room, so apply_terminal_layout puts your panels back on the same wall every time you walk in.
entries.how: get_terminal_layouts and apply_terminal_layout already exist and answer 'unavailable', because TODO.md notes that '/term pin' has no absolute world-position form. This needs that form in GhosttyDalamud first, then layouts keyed by get_housing_info's ward, plot and room, written through the layout.get/layout.set verbs that SiblingIpcProposals.cs leaves out today.
entries.risks: The blocking work is in another mod and has to be designed there. Housing interiors share coordinates across plots, so the key must include the house identity. The sibling IPC patches have not been applied or built. Panels have no depth test and show through walls.

entries.title: GPose Terminal Studio
entries.pitch: Terminals stay in group pose as frozen props you can scroll back, move, tilt or attach to a character's hand.
entries.how: Set DisableGposeUiHide; confirm draw callbacks and ViewProjection follow the GPose camera. Freeze via Session:sleep. Drag/rotate gizmo on world_hit/world_unproject. Hand attach via a GetBone shim forward reading hkaPose and a Lua 'bone' anchor.
entries.risks: ImGui overlays never get game DoF or lighting and cover other actors. The game's screenshot likely excludes Dalamud's layer. Bone math breaks on ClientStructs changes.

entries.title: Kana on the Curve
entries.pitch: IME composition text renders inline at the cursor, even on curved world panels, with a game-styled candidate list.
entries.how: Committed text and wide cells already work. Shim hooks WM_IME_COMPOSITION/ImmGetCompositionString (or reflects into Dalamud) to forward preedit and cursor. render.nelua draws the underlined overlay in the same draw range so world_transform_vertices curves it. Candidate frame is ImGui; merge a CJK font subset.
entries.risks: CJK at 40px bloats the atlas; ImWchar is 16-bit so no astral characters. IME through Wine/Proton on Linux is unreliable. WndProc hooks can conflict with Dalamud's IME.

entries.title: Ask the Local Model for a Name
entries.pitch: When cover matching fails, ask your own local model through Almanac for the game's canonical name, and keep the answer only if it really exists in the console's list.
entries.how: This is the TODO already written in docs/ARCADE.md. The helper writes unmatched names and their console's cached Named_Boxarts list to state.json; the plugin sends each to Almanac.Ask with a narrow prompt; the answer goes back through a new helper verb and art_match accepts it only if it is exactly one entry in that list. XivMcp stays out of it, as the doc says.
entries.risks: Needs a request and response bridge between the in-game IPC and the host helper, which is why it was left out. Small local models invent names; the exact-list check makes that safe but may leave most games unmatched. Slow on modest GPUs, so it must run in the background and be cancellable.

entries.title: Lyrics, Where Licensed
entries.pitch: Show the words of the song that is playing, if a licensed source that allows it can be found.
entries.how: Pandora's partner API that pianobar documents has no lyrics call, and Pandora's own apps show lyrics from a licensed provider through their private web API, which XivPiano does not use. So this would mean a lyrics provider whose terms allow a third-party player to show them, keyed on Track.Title and Track.Artist, shown in a tab in MainWindow.
entries.risks: Lyrics are licensed separately from the music. Scraping them from lyrics sites, or lifting Pandora's own, would break someone's terms and their licence, which is why this is marked unsafe as it stands. It is listed to see whether people want it enough to look for a proper licence; without one it will not be built.
